tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.

There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. - **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

# B0 merge readiness

Status: **NOT MERGED. Blocked on governance: no eligible human code-owner reviewer exists, and GitHub does not enforce the documented branch protection on `master`.** Engineering verification is complete.

Verified 2026-11-20 by an agent. Model review is not human approval and has not been presented as one.

## State

| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| PR | #155, draft, open, `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95` -> `master` |
| PR head | `173714ed52a279856b3c7c59de6516ce6fd9187f` (only change since the last fully green head `a82a605` is this document) |
| Master | `4c399b87e833b12d15791f6b5f8b08ab35871667` (merge of #154); merge base equals master, branch is 0 behind / 41 ahead |
| Reviews | none; no review requests; 0 review threads, 0 unresolved |
| Mergeable | `MERGEABLE` |

## CI on the final head

Workflows triggered by `pull_request` on `173714e`: CI run 44719629619, Security 44719629455, CodeQL 44719629730. All 21 required check contexts in `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` now report `success`.

Cross-browser Smoke was cancelled on the first attempt: the job sat in `npx playwright install --with-deps firefox webkit` until the job timeout (25 min) and the runner killed it. No test ran. The commit only changed this document, and the same job passed on `a82a605`. The failed job was re-run once without changes and passed (attempt 2, started 11:29 UTC). Diagnosis: transient runner/package-mirror stall, not a code defect.

## Migration 0090

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence | `0090_expansion_domain_release_guard_hardening` is journal idx 90, `when` strictly after 0089; the shared plan's last admin range runs through 90 | `admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, `scripts/shared-migration-plan.json` |
| Checksum | committed blob sha256 `b9a0dbb7…c1c9` matches `scripts/migration-checksums.json` | `git show HEAD:<file> \| sha256sum` |
| Repository gates | `check-migrations`, `check-shared-migration-plan` (115 migrations), `check-migration-history` (52 historical + 63 forward locked) pass locally; the same gates pass in CI | local run, CI `Database and Migrations` |
| Fresh database | CI applies 0090 on every integration database and on the dedicated `postgres-expansion` service, then the restricted-role privilege verifier passes | CI job log (run 44717578398 on `a82a605`, identical migrations) |
| Concurrency on the migrated schema | 89/89, 0 skipped, run as `scalesmiths_expansion_admin` / `scalesmiths_expansion_web` after 0090 was applied; the step fails on any skipped test | same job log |
| Upgrade from a checkpoint-5 (0089) database with history | Passed. The migrator applied only 0090. Of 55 snapshotted tables, the only change was the admin migration journal (90 -> 91 rows); all 53 `expansion_*` tables (for example 214 opportunities, 2 with released domains, 194 commission-ledger rows) kept identical row counts and content digests. Privilege verification passed before and after. Concurrency suite on the upgraded schema: 88/89, the one failure being the collation-dependent test described below (also failed identically on the 0089 schema; passes in CI) | isolated `postgres:16` container, see below |
| Guard behaviour after upgrade | INSERT of a released row refused (new in 0090); rewriting or clearing a recorded release refused; direct release of a non-withdrawn prospect refused; release without a reason refused | `checks-0090.sql` against the upgraded database |
| Founder-controlled release | founder-only, reason required, idempotent replay, audited `domain_released` event, permanent history, suppression still applies; a partner is refused | concurrency test "a founder can release the domain held by an excluded, released candidate" |
| Restricted principals | `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` passes before and after 0090 on the isolated database, and in CI | local and CI logs |

The supplied `database-migration-logs.zip` ended at `admin/0089`; it was not used as evidence for 0090.

Isolated upgrade method: a detached worktree at `173714e`; a disposable `postgres:16` container; shared migrator run with 0090 temporarily removed from the journal and plan (worktree only, restored afterwards, never committed); history seeded by running the concurrency suite on the 0089 schema; a per-table row count and content digest of every `expansion_*` table taken; 0090 applied by the normal migrator; the digest repeated and compared; the concurrency suite re-run on the upgraded schema.

## Remediation review

| Finding | Status on the final head |
|---|---|
| Geographic exclusivity | Fixed in 0088: founder-approved `expansion_areas` tree; containment comes from the tree, not wording; unclassified wording goes to review (fail-closed). Covered by the 5B geography test. |
| Public profile entitlement | Fixed in 0089: the security-barrier view requires a live webpage reward, a current qualified-client count at or above its milestone, and no open qualification flag. Suspension is automatic on the next request; records are kept; a founder restoring entitlement restores the page. Covered by the 5E tests. |
| Released-candidate domain lock | Fixed in 0088 + 0090: founder-only, audited, permanent release for a withdrawn, unworked prospect from an excluded candidate; 0090 makes the database guard match the owner guard and cover INSERT. |
| Concurrency suite in CI | Fixed: `ci.yml` adds a `postgres-expansion` service and two steps; runs as restricted roles; fails if any test is skipped. |

No critical or high findings remain from the agent review. One low-severity test-portability issue: two tests (`expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts:686`, `expansion-finance.test.ts:315`) select `amount_pence::text` and `ORDER BY amount_pence`, which sorts the text output column. It passes on CI's `postgres:16-alpine` and failed once on a Debian `postgres:16` (`en_US.utf8`) because that collation ignores the minus sign (confirmed: `ORDER BY v DESC` gives `-6000,30000` under `en_US.utf8` and `30000,-6000` under `C`). No production query in `admin/src` or `web/src` uses the pattern. Recommended follow-up, not a B0 blocker.

Protected flags default to `false` in `.env.example`. `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_PROFILE_PUBLICATION_ENABLED`, `PUBLIC_PARTNER_PROFILES_ENABLED` and `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED` are read with `=== "true"`, so anything else is closed. Withdrawals additionally need a founder-enabled commercial plan.

## Deployment impact of merging

Merging runs CI, Security and CodeQL on `master` (push trigger). No workflow deploys, uses an environment, or connects to a server; the repository has no deployment environments or webhooks. Production deployment is a separate, manual release-manager operation (`docs/operations/release-runbook.md`). Not verified: any host-side automation outside GitHub (for example a scheduled pull on the VPS).

## Blockers

1. **No eligible human code-owner reviewer.** `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns every path to `@TheFridey`, the PR author and the repository's only collaborator. GitHub does not allow an author to approve their own PR, so the required code-owner approval cannot be given by anyone.
2. **Branch protection is documented but not applied.** `GET /repos/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/branches/master/protection` returns `404 Branch not protected`, and the repository has no rulesets. `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` (1 approval, code-owner review, last-push approval, conversation resolution, up-to-date branch, 20 required checks) is therefore not enforced. A merge would technically succeed today; that is exactly why it was not attempted.
3. PR is still a draft.

## Proposed resolution (repository owner only)

The agent has not changed repository settings and will not.

1. Add a trusted second person as a collaborator with write access, and list them in `CODEOWNERS` for the protected paths (at least `admin/drizzle/`, `.github/`, the restricted-role scripts and the Expansion server code).
2. Apply `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` to `master` (classic protection or a ruleset), and confirm `check-branch-protection-policy.mjs` reports no drift.
3. That reviewer reviews against the checklist below and approves after the final push.
4. Owner marks the PR ready, confirms deployment impact, and merges.

If the owner instead chooses a documented solo-maintainer exception, that is the owner's decision, should be recorded in `docs/operations/protected-areas-and-branch-protection.md`, and still does not make an agent or model review count as approval.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] **Migrations 0073-0090**: forward-only, none rewritten, journal/plan/checksums agree; 0088 area tree and domain release columns; 0089 view; 0090 guard (INSERT path, permanent history). Rollback is restore-from-backup, not down-migrations.
- [ ] **Financial invariants**: commission is never paid from conditional rewards; refunds adjust unpaid or reserved commission; negative adjustments travel with withdrawals; no double allocation under contention; ledger and audit append-only.
- [ ] **PostgreSQL privileges**: web role reads only the security-barrier view; admin runtime role cannot migrate or own schema; `provision-postgres-roles.mjs` and `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` agree.
- [ ] **Public profile view**: only live, consented, approved content of an active partner with current entitlement; no private columns; partner self-takedown.
- [ ] **Exclusivity**: area-tree containment, fail-closed review for unclassified wording, partner requests never evaluated against exclusivity.
- [ ] **Domain allocation and release**: single holder under races; release founder-only, reasoned, audited, permanent; suppression unaffected.
- [ ] **CI workflow**: `postgres-expansion` service, CI-only credentials, skip guard; no new secrets, permissions or deploy steps.
- [ ] **Production deployment triggers**: none in GitHub; confirm no host-side automation.
- [ ] **Rollback**: restore the pre-migration backup; keep all partner flags unset.

## After a permitted merge

Verify the merge commit and its tree on `master`, inspect `master` CI, confirm every protected flag above remains unset in production configuration, and confirm no deployment occurred. Do not activate partner intake, public profiles, withdrawals or rewards. B1 (Operation Empower) must not begin until this is recorded.

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Contents

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [PLATFORM-AUDIT.md](PLATFORM-AUDIT.md) | The existing systems Empower reuses, with file references and gaps |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | Proposed data model, content lifecycle, deterministic search and integration points |
| [SECURITY-MODEL.md](SECURITY-MODEL.md) | Roles, audience separation, publication controls, threats and mitigations |
| [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) | The 13 Academy courses: objectives, modules, lesson outlines, knowledge checks, resources and review requirements |
| [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 1 to 6 (company and services) |
| [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 7 to 13 (selling, policy and conduct) |
| [resources/README.md](resources/README.md) | The 13 Resource Centre drafts, one file each |
| [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md) | Approved-content architecture and the knowledge article inventory |
| [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md) | Visual language, tokens and components, reconciled with the existing design systems |
| [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md) | Wireframe descriptions for the seven key screens |
| [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) | Every item in this package with its approval status, owner and blocking effect |
| [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md) | Proposed delivery phases and their entry and exit gates |
| [ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md](ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md) | Testable acceptance criteria for each phase |

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

## Relationship to existing registers

This package extends, and does not replace, the B0 registers:

- [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md): commercial, legal and operational decisions;
- [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md): content not yet written (much of which this package now drafts);
- [COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md): release modes and gates.

When the founders approve an Empower item, record it in [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) and, where it resolves a row there, in the matching B0 register.
# Platform audit: reusable systems for Empower

**Status: DRAFT.** Audited against B0 head `4e713e5` (branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`). Facts below are `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` unless marked otherwise. Anything not inspected is marked "not verified".

## Summary

The B0 Partner Portal already has the essential primitives for a Resource Centre: a versioned, immutable, audience-tagged resource table with a database-enforced publication lifecycle, a founder publishing form, a partner search box and an onboarding toolkit item reserved for the Academy. What is missing is structure (courses, lessons, knowledge articles with fields), approval evidence (who approved which version, and when it must be reviewed again), progress tracking and a proper search index. Empower should **extend these patterns, not replace them**.

## 1. Partner Portal (admin app, `/partner`)

| Aspect | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Location | Lives on the existing admin origin. No separate subdomain or authentication stack | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` (`partnerLoginUrl`), `admin/src/app/partner/page.tsx` |
| Role | `independent_partner` holds exactly one capability, `expansion.partner` | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:28` |
| Route guard | `/partner` and `/partner/*` map to `expansion.partner`; `/api/partner*` is the only API family that capability reaches | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:53`, `:99` |
| Workspace | One client component with tabs: Overview, Prospects & scope, Resource library, Commission centre, Achievements, My web page, Referrals, Onboarding, Meetings | `admin/src/components/expansion/ExpansionWorkspace.tsx:67` |
| Styling | Scoped `ex-*` classes in `expansion.css`: panels, badges, `details`-based resource rows, list rows | `admin/src/components/expansion/expansion.css` |
| Server guard | Partner reads run in a transaction behind `requireCapability("expansion.partner")` and `partnerGuard`, which share-locks the user row | `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts:31-52` |

**Reuse:** add Academy and Resource Centre as new workspace areas (or child routes under `/partner`) behind the same capability. **Gap:** the workspace is a single large component; new areas should be separate route segments so they can be code-split and tested independently (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)).

## 2. Founder administration (`/expansion`)

- Route `/expansion` requires `expansion.manage`; founder-only actions use `expansion.founder`. Owner and administrator roles exclude `expansion.partner`, so a founder account never doubles as a partner (`admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:26-27`).
- The founder workspace already includes Recruitment, Programme, Partner operations, Research and allocation, Recognition, Web pages and Delivery capacity tabs.
- Every write goes through one command endpoint (`admin/src/app/api/expansion/route.ts`) and writes an audit row (`audit(tx, actor.id, id, 'resource_created', …)` in `admin/src/lib/server/expansion.ts:279`).

**Reuse:** the founder publishing interface belongs here, as a new "Content" area using the same command and audit pattern.

## 3. Existing resource system

| Aspect | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Table | `expansion_resources(id, title, category, version, audience ∈ {partner, client}, content, status ∈ {draft, published, archived}, created_by, created_at)` | `admin/drizzle/0068_expansion_foundation.sql:46-51` |
| Immutability | A trigger refuses deletes and any change to content fields. Content changes need a new version | `admin/drizzle/0070_expansion_cancellations.sql:8-15` |
| Lifecycle | Only `draft → published`, `draft → archived` and `published → archived` are allowed, in both the trigger and the service | same, and `admin/src/lib/server/expansion.ts:282-288` |
| Partner read | Only `status='published' AND audience='partner'` rows reach the partner snapshot (filtered on the server) | `admin/src/lib/server/expansion.ts:118` |
| Rendering | Plain text with `white-space: pre-wrap` (`ex-prewrap`). No Markdown or HTML rendering, so no injection surface today | `ExpansionWorkspace.tsx:77` |
| Search | Client-side substring match over title and content, plus a category filter | `ExpansionWorkspace.tsx:28-29`, `:77` |
| Limits | Title 200 characters, category 100, content 30,000 | `expansion.ts:278` |
| Client audience | No consumer of `audience='client'` rows was found in `web/src` (searched for `expansion_resources`). Client-facing resources therefore have no delivery route today | search result, not exhaustively verified |

**Gaps for Empower:**

1. There is no approval evidence: `published` records who created a row, not who approved it, against what source or until when. Empower needs an approval record per version, with reviewer, date, source references and review-by date.
2. There is no `superseded_by` link, so partners cannot tell which version is current within a family of versions.

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

# Empower architecture (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** This is a design proposal for engineering review after B0 merges. No table, route or migration described here exists. Migration numbers are not reserved.

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

1. Partners can find approved answers, resources and training quickly, and can tell at a glance what is approved, for whom, and until when.
2. Founders can draft, review, approve, publish, supersede and retire every content item, with evidence and an audit trail.
3. Partner-only and client-facing material can never be confused or cross-published by accident.
4. The Academy is optional and voluntary, and progress never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing.

**Non-goals for B1 and the first build**

- No AI generation, AI answers, embeddings or paid AI APIs.
- No assessment that gates anything, no certification, no leaderboard.
- No file uploads, video hosting or third-party learning platform.
- No change to commission, markets, exclusivity or any B0 financial path.
- No client portal delivery of client-facing resources (a later, separate decision).

## 2. Building blocks

```
            Founder administration (/expansion → Content)                Partner Portal (/partner)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Draft editor → Review → Approve → Publish        │      │ Academy   Resources   Knowledge search  │
  │ Supersede / Archive / Review-due queue           │      │ Objection workspace   My progress       │
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘      └───────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                  │ expansion.founder (writes)                                  │ expansion.partner (reads)
                  ▼                                                             ▼
        content service (server only)  ──────────── published, partner-audience, in-review-window rows only
                  │
                  ▼
  PostgreSQL: content_items · content_versions · content_approvals · content_links
              academy_courses · academy_modules · academy_lessons · academy_progress
              knowledge_entries · search documents (tsvector)
```

All reads and writes go through server functions in the admin app, following the existing `requireCapability` and `partnerGuard` pattern in `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts`. There is no client-supplied filter on audience or status.

## 3. Proposed data model

The model generalises `expansion_resources` (immutable versions, database-enforced lifecycle) and adds approval evidence modelled on the public-claims registry (`verifiedAt`, `reviewExpiresAt`, permitted placement).

### 3.1 Content families and versions

| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `empower_content_items` | A stable identity for one piece of content across versions (for example "Objection: too expensive") | `id`, `kind ∈ {resource, lesson, knowledge, objection, template}`, `slug` (unique), `audience ∈ {partner_only, client_facing}`, `owner_role`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_versions` | Immutable content. Never updated except `status`; never deleted | `id`, `item_id`, `version` (unique per item), `title`, `body` (restricted Markdown), `fields jsonb` (kind-specific, validated), `source_refs jsonb` (list of repository paths or approved documents), `status ∈ {draft, in_review, approved, published, superseded, archived}`, `created_by`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_approvals` | Append-only approval evidence | `id`, `version_id`, `decision ∈ {approved, changes_requested, rejected}`, `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `reference` (founder decision reference), `review_by date`, `notes` |
| `empower_content_links` | Typed relationships | `from_item`, `to_item`, `relation ∈ {supports_lesson, see_also, escalates_to, replaces}` |

Lifecycle, enforced by a trigger like `expansion_resource_lifecycle`:

```
draft ──► in_review ──► approved ──► published ──► superseded
  │           │                         │
  └──► archived ◄──────── changes ──────┴──► archived
```

- `in_review → approved` requires an `empower_content_approvals` row with `decision='approved'` by a user holding `expansion.founder`, and it must be a **different** founder from the version's author when two founders are active (founder decision `AP-GOV-04`).
- `approved → published` is a separate action, so approval and release can be scheduled apart.
- Publishing version N of an item moves the previously published version to `superseded` in the same transaction. There is at most one published version per item (partial unique index).
- A published version whose `review_by` date has passed is **not served to partners** (fail closed) and appears in the founder "review due" queue. This mirrors `reviewExpiresAt` in `web/src/lib/public-claims.ts`.
- `audience` belongs to the item, not the version, so a new version cannot quietly change who sees it. Changing audience means creating a new item.

### 3.2 Academy

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `empower_courses` | Course identity, order, summary, `content_item_id` for its description |
| `empower_modules` | Ordered modules within a course |
| `empower_lessons` | Ordered lessons; each points at a lesson `content_item` (so lesson text uses the same versioning and approval) |
| `empower_knowledge_checks` | Optional questions per lesson, stored in the lesson version's `fields` |
| `empower_progress` | `partner_id`, `lesson_item_id`, `version_id` read, `opened_at`, `completed_at`, `check_attempted bool` |

Rules:

- **Progress is private to the partner** and visible to founders only in aggregate (counts per course), unless the partner chooses to share it (founder decision `AP-GOV-03`). Progress has no foreign key to, or query from, any commission, allocation, recognition or achievement table, matching the meetings design in [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored, only "attempted". No score is persisted.
- When a lesson is superseded, progress stays attached to the version that was read, and the lesson shows "updated since you read it".

### 3.3 Knowledge entries

A knowledge entry is a `content_item` of kind `knowledge`. Its version `fields` hold the required structure from [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md):

```json
{
  "question": "string",
  "answer": "string (partner-facing, precise)",
  "client_explanation": "string (safe to say to a client)",
  "sources": ["web/src/lib/faq-library.ts#hosting-provided"],
  "limitations": "string",
  "escalation": { "required": "always | when | never", "condition": "string", "route": "technical_scoping | commercial_assistance | escalation | …" },
  "aliases": ["other ways people ask it"],
  "topic": "hosting"
}
```

The service validates the shape on write. A knowledge version without a source, limitation or escalation rule cannot move to `in_review`.

## 4. Search: deterministic first

**Recommendation: PostgreSQL full-text search with curated synonyms and exact alias matching. No embeddings, no language model.**

Why:

- Every answer a partner sees must be approved text. Retrieval that returns approved items verbatim is auditable; generated answers are not.
- No AI provider, budget or data-processing agreement is approved ([FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md)).
- The corpus is small (hundreds of items). PostgreSQL search is fast at that size, already in the stack, and adds no dependency.
- Results are reproducible, so they can be tested.

Design:

1. On publish, the service writes a search document for the version: `setweight(to_tsvector('english', title || question), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', aliases), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', answer || body), 'B') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', topic), 'C')`. A generated column or a row written in the same transaction keeps it consistent.
2. A founder-managed synonym list (`empower_search_synonyms`: term → canonical term, for example "ssl" → "https certificate", "aeo" → "ai search", "wp" → "wordpress") expands the query before `websearch_to_tsquery`. This is deterministic and reviewable.
3. Ranking: exact alias match first, then `ts_rank_cd` with weights, then topic order. Ties broken by slug, so ordering is stable.
4. Filtering in SQL, never in the browser: `status='published' AND review_by >= current_date AND audience` permitted for the caller.
5. Zero-result queries are logged (query text only, partner id hashed) so founders can see gaps and add aliases. Retention for this log is a founder decision (`AP-PRIV-02`).
6. Optional later step: `pg_trgm` for typo tolerance. It is still deterministic.

What would justify revisiting: a corpus of thousands of items, evidence from zero-result logs that synonyms cannot keep up, and an approved AI provider and data-processing agreement. Even then, the answer shown should be an approved entry, with retrieval-only assistance.

## 5. Rendering

- Bodies are a **restricted Markdown subset**: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, tables, block quotes and links to internal routes or approved external domains. Raw HTML is disabled. Rendering happens on the server, with a sanitising pass as defence in depth.
- Client-facing items render with a visible "Client-facing: approved for sharing" ribbon. Partner-only items render with "Partner only: do not share".
- Every rendered item shows version, approval date and review-by date.
- Copy-to-clipboard is offered only for client-facing items and templates.

## 6. Integration with B0

| B0 system | Integration |
|---|---|
| `expansion_resources` | Keep as is. Migrate existing published rows into `empower_content_items` as `kind='resource'` in Phase 1, or leave them read-only and stop creating new ones. Decision `AP-ENG-01` |
| Onboarding toolkit | Link published handbook, brochure, pricing and commission references to `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents` and `academy` items. Requires the toolkit join to accept Empower items (small change) or the content to remain mirrored in `expansion_resources` |
| Meetings | Every escalation rule names a meeting type. "Request help" in the knowledge viewer opens the existing meeting request form pre-filled with the type and a reference to the entry |
| Audit | Every content write calls the existing `audit()` helper with an `empower_*` event name |
| RBAC | No new role. Reads: `expansion.partner`. Writes and approvals: `expansion.founder`. Founder preview uses the partner renderer with a "preview" banner |
| `partner-programme.ts` | Commercial lessons and the commission reference embed figures by **reference** to the programme constants, rendered with the plan version they come from, so they cannot drift from the engine |

## 7. Feature flags

Following the B0 pattern (everything defaults off):

| Flag | Default | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Resource Centre and knowledge search |
| `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Academy |
| `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` | `false` in production until Phase 1 is accepted | Founder content workspace |

With a flag off, partner routes return 404 and the tab is hidden. The founder workspace can be enabled first so content can be loaded and approved before partners see anything.

## 8. Open engineering decisions

| ID | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `AP-ENG-01` | Migrate or freeze `expansion_resources` | Freeze: keep it for toolkit links, create new content in Empower tables, add a read adapter |
| `AP-ENG-02` | Markdown renderer | A small, maintained renderer with HTML disabled; justify the dependency in the PR |
| `AP-ENG-03` | Separate routes or tabs | Separate route segments under `/partner/academy`, `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge`, sharing the portal shell |
| `AP-ENG-04` | Content seeding | A reviewed seed script that loads drafts from this folder as `draft` versions only, never as published |
# Empower security model (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Extends [../SECURITY-MODEL.md](../SECURITY-MODEL.md) and the B0 hardening work. Nothing here changes authentication.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Partner-only content (commission references, objection playbooks, escalation routes) | Internal | Leakage could be read as a commercial offer or misused by competitors |
| Client-facing content | Low once approved; high while draft | A leaked draft could be presented to a client as approved |
| Approval records | Integrity-critical | They are the evidence that content was approved |
| Partner progress | Personal data | Could be used to monitor or direct partners, which bears on independent status |
| Search logs | Personal data (low) | Reveal what an individual partner is working on |

## 2. Roles and capabilities

No new role or capability is required.

| Actor | Capability | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent partner | `expansion.partner` | Read published, in-review-window content for their audience; search; record own progress; request a meeting from an entry | See drafts, approvals, other partners' progress, founder notes or search logs; write content |
| Founder | `expansion.manage` + `expansion.founder` | Draft, review, approve, publish, supersede, archive; see aggregate progress; preview as partner | Approve their own draft when two founders are active (decision `AP-GOV-04`); delete versions |
| Owner, administrator | per `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts` | Whatever their existing capabilities allow | They never hold `expansion.partner`, so they cannot act as a partner |
| Anonymous | none | Nothing | Reach any Empower route (the admin origin requires sign-in) |

## 3. Controls

### 3.1 Audience separation

- Audience is set on the **item**, cannot change, and is checked in SQL on every read.
- Partner-only items carry a "Partner only: do not share" ribbon and no copy button. Client-facing items carry an approval ribbon with the version and date.
- A lint rule in the content service refuses to move a `client_facing` version to `in_review` if its body contains blocked terms (commission, basis points, payout, withdrawal, referral reward, founder-only, internal) unless a founder explicitly overrides with a reason. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.

### 3.2 Publication integrity

- Immutable versions, enforced by a trigger (same approach as `expansion_resource_lifecycle`).
- Approval is a separate, append-only row recorded by a founder, with a reference and a review-by date.
- Publication fails closed: an expired review date, a missing approval or a disabled flag means the item is not served.
- Every transition writes an audit row with the actor and the version id.

### 3.3 Rendering safety

- Restricted Markdown, raw HTML disabled, server-side rendering, then sanitising.
- Links are limited to internal routes and an allow-list of external domains (for example `ico.org.uk`, `gov.uk`). Founders manage the allow-list.
- No file uploads in this scope, so there is no malware-scanning or storage requirement. Photographs remain unsupported, as in B0.

### 3.4 Input handling

- Every write goes through the existing command endpoint pattern with length limits (B0 uses 200 for titles and 30,000 for content).
- `fields` JSON is validated against a schema per `kind` on the server.
- Search input is length-limited (200 characters), passed as a bound parameter to `websearch_to_tsquery`, and rate-limited per partner (the public site's `web/src/lib/rate-limit-policy.ts` is the model; an admin-side equivalent was not verified).

### 3.5 Independence and privacy

- Progress is private to the partner by default. Founders see aggregates only, unless the partner chooses to share (decision `AP-GOV-03`).
- No progress, completion or knowledge-check data is joined to commission, allocation, recognition or achievements. A test should assert that no such query exists.
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored.
- Search logs: query text and a hashed partner id, retained for a founder-approved period (decision `AP-PRIV-02`). The privacy notice must mention them (decision `AP-PRIV-01`).

## 4. Threats and mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|
| A partner presents a draft as approved | Partners never receive drafts; every rendered item shows approval metadata | A partner could paraphrase from memory; covered by the Professional Conduct course and the partner agreement |
| Partner-only commission information reaches a client | Audience on item, lint check, ribbons, no copy button | A partner can still screenshot; agreement and training cover this |
| A stale price or policy is quoted | Review-by dates fail closed; commercial figures embedded by reference to programme constants | A partner may have saved an old copy; versions show "updated since" |
| A founder approves their own mistake | Second-founder approval rule; audit trail | Single-founder periods need an explicit override with a reason |
| Stored XSS through content | No raw HTML, server rendering, sanitiser, link allow-list | Renderer dependency must be kept patched |
| Progress used to direct or monitor partners | Private by default, no joins to commercial tables, voluntary framing | Requires founder discipline and solicitor review (`AP-GOV-02`) |
| Search probing reveals hidden content | Search runs only over published, permitted rows; zero results look the same whether content is hidden or absent | None identified |
| Enumeration of other partners' data | All partner queries keyed by the authenticated actor via `partnerGuard` | None identified |

## 5. Verification expected at implementation

- Service tests for every lifecycle transition, including refusals.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests for the trigger and the one-published-version index, as B0 does for its guards.
- Role tests: a partner cannot reach any founder content action; an owner cannot reach partner routes.
- A browser test that a partner sees no draft, no expired item and no client-facing copy control on partner-only items.
- A test asserting progress tables are not referenced by commercial queries.

2. A founder-managed synonym list (`empower_search_synonyms`: term → canonical term, for example "ssl" → "https certificate", "aeo" → "ai search", "wp" → "wordpress") expands the query before `websearch_to_tsquery`. This is deterministic and reviewable.
3. Ranking: exact alias match first, then `ts_rank_cd` with weights, then topic order. Ties broken by slug, so ordering is stable.
4. Filtering in SQL, never in the browser: `status='published' AND review_by >= current_date AND audience` permitted for the caller.
5. Zero-result queries are logged (query text only, partner id hashed) so founders can see gaps and add aliases. Retention for this log is a founder decision (`AP-PRIV-02`).
6. Optional later step: `pg_trgm` for typo tolerance. It is still deterministic.

What would justify revisiting: a corpus of thousands of items, evidence from zero-result logs that synonyms cannot keep up, and an approved AI provider and data-processing agreement. Even then, the answer shown should be an approved entry, with retrieval-only assistance.

## 5. Rendering

- Bodies are a **restricted Markdown subset**: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, tables, block quotes and links to internal routes or approved external domains. Raw HTML is disabled. Rendering happens on the server, with a sanitising pass as defence in depth.
- Client-facing items render with a visible "Client-facing: approved for sharing" ribbon. Partner-only items render with "Partner only: do not share".
- Every rendered item shows version, approval date and review-by date.
- Copy-to-clipboard is offered only for client-facing items and templates.

## 6. Integration with B0

| B0 system | Integration |
|---|---|
| `expansion_resources` | Keep as is. Migrate existing published rows into `empower_content_items` as `kind='resource'` in Phase 1, or leave them read-only and stop creating new ones. Decision `AP-ENG-01` |
| Onboarding toolkit | Link published handbook, brochure, pricing and commission references to `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents` and `academy` items. Requires the toolkit join to accept Empower items (small change) or the content to remain mirrored in `expansion_resources` |
| Meetings | Every escalation rule names a meeting type. "Request help" in the knowledge viewer opens the existing meeting request form pre-filled with the type and a reference to the entry |
| Audit | Every content write calls the existing `audit()` helper with an `empower_*` event name |
| RBAC | No new role. Reads: `expansion.partner`. Writes and approvals: `expansion.founder`. Founder preview uses the partner renderer with a "preview" banner |
| `partner-programme.ts` | Commercial lessons and the commission reference embed figures by **reference** to the programme constants, rendered with the plan version they come from, so they cannot drift from the engine |

## 7. Feature flags

Following the B0 pattern (everything defaults off):

| Flag | Default | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Resource Centre and knowledge search |
| `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Academy |
| `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` | `false` in production until Phase 1 is accepted | Founder content workspace |

With a flag off, partner routes return 404 and the tab is hidden. The founder workspace can be enabled first so content can be loaded and approved before partners see anything.

## 8. Open engineering decisions

| ID | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `AP-ENG-01` | Migrate or freeze `expansion_resources` | Freeze: keep it for toolkit links, create new content in Empower tables, add a read adapter |
| `AP-ENG-02` | Markdown renderer | A small, maintained renderer with HTML disabled; justify the dependency in the PR |
| `AP-ENG-03` | Separate routes or tabs | Separate route segments under `/partner/academy`, `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge`, sharing the portal shell |
| `AP-ENG-04` | Content seeding | A reviewed seed script that loads drafts from this folder as `draft` versions only, never as published |
# Empower security model (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Extends [../SECURITY-MODEL.md](../SECURITY-MODEL.md) and the B0 hardening work. Nothing here changes authentication.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Partner-only content (commission references, objection playbooks, escalation routes) | Internal | Leakage could be read as a commercial offer or misused by competitors |
| Client-facing content | Low once approved; high while draft | A leaked draft could be presented to a client as approved |
| Approval records | Integrity-critical | They are the evidence that content was approved |
| Partner progress | Personal data | Could be used to monitor or direct partners, which bears on independent status |
| Search logs | Personal data (low) | Reveal what an individual partner is working on |

## 2. Roles and capabilities

No new role or capability is required.

| Actor | Capability | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent partner | `expansion.partner` | Read published, in-review-window content for their audience; search; record own progress; request a meeting from an entry | See drafts, approvals, other partners' progress, founder notes or search logs; write content |
| Founder | `expansion.manage` + `expansion.founder` | Draft, review, approve, publish, supersede, archive; see aggregate progress; preview as partner | Approve their own draft when two founders are active (decision `AP-GOV-04`); delete versions |
| Owner, administrator | per `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts` | Whatever their existing capabilities allow | They never hold `expansion.partner`, so they cannot act as a partner |
| Anonymous | none | Nothing | Reach any Empower route (the admin origin requires sign-in) |

## 3. Controls

### 3.1 Audience separation

- Audience is set on the **item**, cannot change, and is checked in SQL on every read.
- Partner-only items carry a "Partner only: do not share" ribbon and no copy button. Client-facing items carry an approval ribbon with the version and date.
- A lint rule in the content service refuses to move a `client_facing` version to `in_review` if its body contains blocked terms (commission, basis points, payout, withdrawal, referral reward, founder-only, internal) unless a founder explicitly overrides with a reason. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.

### 3.2 Publication integrity

- Immutable versions, enforced by a trigger (same approach as `expansion_resource_lifecycle`).
- Approval is a separate, append-only row recorded by a founder, with a reference and a review-by date.
- Publication fails closed: an expired review date, a missing approval or a disabled flag means the item is not served.
- Every transition writes an audit row with the actor and the version id.

### 3.3 Rendering safety

- Restricted Markdown, raw HTML disabled, server-side rendering, then sanitising.
- Links are limited to internal routes and an allow-list of external domains (for example `ico.org.uk`, `gov.uk`). Founders manage the allow-list.
- No file uploads in this scope, so there is no malware-scanning or storage requirement. Photographs remain unsupported, as in B0.

### 3.4 Input handling

- Every write goes through the existing command endpoint pattern with length limits (B0 uses 200 for titles and 30,000 for content).
- `fields` JSON is validated against a schema per `kind` on the server.
- Search input is length-limited (200 characters), passed as a bound parameter to `websearch_to_tsquery`, and rate-limited per partner (the public site's `web/src/lib/rate-limit-policy.ts` is the model; an admin-side equivalent was not verified).

### 3.5 Independence and privacy

- Progress is private to the partner by default. Founders see aggregates only, unless the partner chooses to share (decision `AP-GOV-03`).
- No progress, completion or knowledge-check data is joined to commission, allocation, recognition or achievements. A test should assert that no such query exists.
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored.
- Search logs: query text and a hashed partner id, retained for a founder-approved period (decision `AP-PRIV-02`). The privacy notice must mention them (decision `AP-PRIV-01`).

## 4. Threats and mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|
| A partner presents a draft as approved | Partners never receive drafts; every rendered item shows approval metadata | A partner could paraphrase from memory; covered by the Professional Conduct course and the partner agreement |
| Partner-only commission information reaches a client | Audience on item, lint check, ribbons, no copy button | A partner can still screenshot; agreement and training cover this |
| A stale price or policy is quoted | Review-by dates fail closed; commercial figures embedded by reference to programme constants | A partner may have saved an old copy; versions show "updated since" |
| A founder approves their own mistake | Second-founder approval rule; audit trail | Single-founder periods need an explicit override with a reason |
| Stored XSS through content | No raw HTML, server rendering, sanitiser, link allow-list | Renderer dependency must be kept patched |
| Progress used to direct or monitor partners | Private by default, no joins to commercial tables, voluntary framing | Requires founder discipline and solicitor review (`AP-GOV-02`) |
| Search probing reveals hidden content | Search runs only over published, permitted rows; zero results look the same whether content is hidden or absent | None identified |
| Enumeration of other partners' data | All partner queries keyed by the authenticated actor via `partnerGuard` | None identified |

## 5. Verification expected at implementation

- Service tests for every lifecycle transition, including refusals.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests for the trigger and the one-published-version index, as B0 does for its guards.
- Role tests: a partner cannot reach any founder content action; an owner cannot reach partner routes.
- A browser test that a partner sees no draft, no expired item and no client-facing copy control on partner-only items.
- A test asserting progress tables are not referenced by commercial queries.

1	# Partner Academy curriculum
2	
3	**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).
4	
5	## Principles
6	
7	- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
8	- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
9	- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
10	- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
11	- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".
12

35	## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

37	**Purpose:** a clear, honest picture of who ScaleSmiths is, what it sells and how the partnership works.

41	2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;
42	3. find approved answers in the Resource Centre and know when to ask for help;
43	4. tell the difference between approved, proposed and planned features.

49	| M1 Who we are | C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words | Based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire; custom builds; published work; how to say it briefly |

51	| | C01-L3 How we work | Discovery, written proposal, phased delivery, evidence over promises |
