# Partner Academy curriculum

**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).

## Principles

- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

## Course map

| # | Course | Modules | Lessons | Audience of content | Review owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Welcome to ScaleSmiths | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C02 | Professional Website Development | 3 | 8 | Partner only (includes client-safe phrasing) | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C03 | SEO and Digital Growth | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C04 | Growth Partnerships | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C05 | Website Migration | 2 | 6 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C06 | Bespoke Software and Automation | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C07 | Finding Prospects | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + privacy adviser | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (marketing process) |
| C08 | Discovery Meetings | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C09 | Presenting ScaleSmiths | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C10 | Objection Handling | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C11 | Commercial Policies | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + accountant + solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement, terms) |
| C12 | Professional Conduct | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + employment solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement) |
| C13 | Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |

Suggested (not required) order: C01, C12, C02, C04, C08, then any.

---

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

**Purpose:** a clear, honest picture of who ScaleSmiths is, what it sells and how the partnership works.

**Learning objectives.** After this course a partner can:
1. describe ScaleSmiths and its services in two sentences without overstating them;
2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;
3. find approved answers in the Resource Centre and know when to ask for help;
4. tell the difference between approved, proposed and planned features.

**Modules and lessons**

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Who we are | C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words | Based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire; custom builds; published work; how to say it briefly |
| | C01-L2 What we sell | Four published offers plus independently scoped custom work; starting-price boundary |
| | C01-L3 How we work | Discovery, written proposal, phased delivery, evidence over promises |
| M2 Your role | C01-L4 What an independent partner does | Introduce, qualify, register, support; ScaleSmiths scopes, prices and delivers |
| | C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned | Reading the availability labels; why nothing is promised |
| M3 Using the portal | C01-L6 Finding answers fast | Knowledge search, resources, approval ribbons, versions |
| | C01-L7 Getting help | Meeting types, escalation, what to send |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions (for example "A prospect asks whether we guarantee first place on Google. What is the approved answer?").

**Supporting resources:** [R01 Company brochure](resources/R01-company-brochure.md), [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md), knowledge entries `KB-COM-01`, `KB-ONB-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm company description and service list (`AP-CNT-01`); confirm the partner role wording matches the final agreement (`AP-GOV-01`); confirm the availability labels at review time.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

**Purpose:** explain ScaleSmiths website projects accurately and recognise a good-fit prospect.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a typical website project includes and excludes;
2. state the published starting price with its boundary;
3. explain hosting, domains, ownership and self-editing at a client-friendly level;
4. recognise when a project is really custom software, e-commerce or migration and route it.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The offer | C02-L1 What a website project includes | Messaging, structure, responsive build, search foundations, enquiry route, launch support |
| | C02-L2 What is separate | Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations, open-ended support |
| | C02-L3 Price and proposal | "From £2,000" and the starting-price boundary; the proposal is the scope |
| M2 Questions clients ask | C02-L4 Timelines | Confirmed after discovery; content readiness drives schedule |
| | C02-L5 Ownership and editing | Ownership follows signed documents and payment; editing is a scoping decision |
| | C02-L6 Technology and WordPress | Custom builds; WordPress is reviewed on its merits (owner review flag) |
| M3 Fit and routing | C02-L7 Good-fit signals | Established business, clear services, evidence to protect |
| | C02-L8 When it is not a standard website | E-commerce, booking, portals, migration → escalate |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), `KB-HOST-*`, `KB-DOM-*`, `KB-ECOM-01`, `KB-BOOK-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm "what is included" list; confirm WordPress wording (source is `ownerReview`); approve use of published project names in partner conversations (`AP-PROOF-01`).

---

**Purpose:** talk about search visibility, including AI search, accurately and without promises.

4. respond to "can you guarantee page one?" with the approved answer.

| | C03-L3 Technical SEO | Crawl, render, canonicals, sitemaps, redirects, Core Web Vitals, HTTPS |
| M2 Honest expectations | C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees | Months, not weeks; no position is promised |
| | C03-L5 Build versus ongoing | Foundations in build; ongoing via project or Growth Partnership |
| | C03-L6 SEO and paid search | Different problems; honest recommendation |
| M3 AI search | C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean | Answer engines, structured content, direct answers; no guarantee of inclusion |
| | C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google" | Indexing, intent mismatch, authority; why audits start in Search Console |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R06 SEO and AEO guide](resources/R06-seo-and-aeo-guide.md), `KB-SEO-*`, `KB-AIS-*`, `KB-ANL-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** approve the AI search lesson (no published FAQ answer exists yet; `AP-CNT-06`); confirm Business Growth Audit positioning.

| | C11-L2 Proposals and payment terms | Terms are per proposal; no blanket deposit policy |
| M2 Partner terms (proposed) | C11-L3 How commission is proposed to work | 30% on eligible collected payments; build plus first Growth Partnership payment |
| | C11-L4 Worked examples | £705 standard; discounted examples; bespoke |
| | C11-L5 What is not decided | Withdrawals, refunds, VAT, achievements, referrals |
| M3 Boundaries | C11-L6 What you may and may not agree | No pricing, discounts, terms or timelines |
| | C11-L7 Markets | No market is approved yet; GBP only |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), [R12 Commission and payment reference](resources/R12-commission-and-payment-reference.md), `KB-TERMS-*`, `KB-PAY-*`, `KB-COMM-*`.

**Founder review requirements:** all items in [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) marked A or F that the course mentions; accountant review of every worked example; solicitor review of wording.

---

## C12 Professional Conduct

**Purpose:** protect clients, partners and ScaleSmiths through honest, lawful and respectful conduct.

**Status note:** `BLOCKED` on the final partner agreement. Wording on independent status must be reviewed by an employment solicitor.

**Learning objectives:**
1. describe the independent partner relationship accurately;
2. represent ScaleSmiths truthfully and within approved material;
3. handle personal data and confidential information properly;
4. handle complaints, conflicts and mistakes.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Your status | C12-L1 Independent, not employed | No salary, guaranteed income, compulsory hours or targets |
| | C12-L2 How to describe yourself | Approved titles; no implied employment, ownership or directorship |
| M2 Honesty | C12-L3 Truthful representation | Approved content only; no guarantees, invented proof or unapproved prices |
| | C12-L4 Pressure and vulnerability | No pressure selling; extra care with vulnerable people |
| M3 Information | C12-L5 Personal data | Collect only what is needed; portal not personal spreadsheets |
| | C12-L6 Confidentiality | Commission, exclusivity and founder information stay private |
| | C12-L7 Complaints and mistakes | Tell ScaleSmiths quickly; never cover up |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md).

**Founder review requirements:** solicitor review of status wording (`AP-GOV-01`, `AP-GOV-02`); privacy adviser review of data handling (`AP-PRIV-01`); approved partner title wording (`AP-GOV-05`).

---

## C13 Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities

**Purpose:** recognise larger and more complex opportunities and bring ScaleSmiths in early.

**Learning objectives:**
1. recognise multi-site, established-organisation and platform opportunities;
2. understand that complex work is scoped after discovery and never sold against a starting price;
3. understand how additional business with an existing client is handled;
4. prepare a strong bespoke discovery request.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Recognising scale | C13-L1 Established business transformation | Multi-site, customer journeys, integrations |
| | C13-L2 Custom platforms and enterprise | Architecture, security, migrations, support |
| M2 How it is handled | C13-L3 Scoped after discovery | No starting price; written scope |
| | C13-L4 Existing clients and additional work | Additional-business claims, attribution evidence (proposed) |
| M3 Your part | C13-L5 Preparing a bespoke discovery request | Information to gather |
| | C13-L6 Joint meetings | When and how to request one |

**Optional knowledge check:** four questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R05 Bespoke software guide](resources/R05-bespoke-software-guide.md), [R10 Technical escalation guide](resources/R10-technical-escalation-guide.md).

**Founder review requirements:** attribution evidence standard (B0 open decision); bespoke eligibility; approve enterprise examples.

1	# Initial lesson content: courses 1 to 6
2	
3	**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published, not for use with partners or clients.** Every lesson needs founder approval before publication (see [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)). Lesson structure is in [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md).
4	
5	Conventions:
6	
7	- **Sources** lists the repository files a lesson relies on. `faq:<key>` means the entry with that key in `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`.
8	- **Say it like this** gives client-safe phrasing taken from published wording.
9	- Text marked *[PROPOSED POLICY]* or *[FOUNDER DECISION]* must keep that label until the decision is recorded.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths
14	
15	### C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words
16	
17	**Sources:** faq:outside-nottingham, faq:established-businesses, faq:wordpress, `web/src/lib/data.ts`.
18	
19	ScaleSmiths is a web and software studio based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire. It works with businesses across the UK and, remotely, with some businesses overseas. Its published work is custom-built: websites and platforms using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes.
20	
21	Most of its client work is with established businesses: organisations that already have customers, a reputation and some evidence (search rankings, enquiries, existing systems) worth protecting. The work usually starts by understanding what already performs before changing anything.
22	
23	What makes ScaleSmiths different is less about technology and more about honesty and accountability. It writes scope down, it does not promise rankings or results it cannot control, and it says plainly when a cheaper or simpler option would serve the client better.
24	
25	**Say it like this:** "ScaleSmiths is a Nottinghamshire web and software studio. They build custom websites and systems for established businesses, and they are very clear about what is included and what is not."
26	
27	**Avoid:** "the best agency", "guaranteed results", "we" (you are not ScaleSmiths staff; see C12), any claim of offices or regional expertise outside what is published.
28	
29	### C01-L2 What we sell
30	
31	**Sources:** `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts`, `web/src/lib/engagement-models.ts`.
32	
33	ScaleSmiths publishes four starting points:
34	
35	| Offer | Published price |
36	|---|---|
37	| Website design and development | From £2,000 |
38	| Growth Partnership | From £350 per month |
39	| Business Growth Audit | £395 |
40	| Managed Business Email | From £15 per month (three 5GB mailboxes, setup included) |
41	
42	It also takes on established-business transformation and custom platforms. These are **never** sold against a website starting price and are scoped after discovery.
43	
44	A starting price is exactly that. The published boundary reads: "A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed result." Prices are in GBP only. ScaleSmiths does not bill in other currencies or publish converted prices.
45	
46	**Rule:** quote only these four figures, always with the boundary. Anything else is a ScaleSmiths proposal.
47	
48	### C01-L3 How we work
49	
50	**Sources:** faq:after-enquiry, faq:timeline, faq:phases, faq:improvement-measurement.
51	
52	1. **Enquiry.** The founders review what is sent and reply with a sensible next step: questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal. Sending a form takes no payment and creates no contract.
53	2. **Discovery.** What the business sells, who buys, how they choose, what the current site does well, and what evidence exists.
54	3. **Written proposal.** Scope, deliverables, delivery range and assumptions, and payment terms.
55	4. **Phased delivery.** A dependable first release; later work follows evidence.
56	5. **Measurement.** Agreed signals, reviewed in conversation, not invented targets.
57	
58	### C01-L4 What an independent partner does
59	
60	**Sources:** `/partners` page copy (`web/src/app/partners/page.tsx`, draft, not approved), [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).
61	
62	As an independent partner you introduce suitable businesses, have early conversations, register prospects in the Partner Portal and support the relationship. ScaleSmiths scopes, prices, contracts and delivers the work.
63	
64	You decide how, when and whether you work. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the final partner agreement defines the relationship. This lesson must be checked against it.]*
65	
66	You do **not**: issue quotes, agree discounts, promise timelines, sign anything on ScaleSmiths' behalf, or handle client payments.
67	
68	### C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned
69	
70	**Sources:** `FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`.
71	
72	The programme uses four labels: **Available subject to approval**, **Planned**, **In development** and **Not available in this market**. Read them literally:
73	
74	- *Available subject to approval* means designed but dependent on the final agreement and approvals.
75	- *Planned* means not built or not operational, with no date.
76	- *In development* means being built, not yet available.
77	
78	In the portal, content carries its own status: only approved, published items are shown, each with a version and review date. If you remember something from a conversation that is not in an approved item, it is not policy.
79	
80	### C01-L6 Finding answers fast
81	
82	Start with knowledge search. Type the question as the client asked it ("do you do hosting?"). Results show approved answers with three parts: the precise answer for you, a client-friendly explanation you may use, and the limitation. If an entry says **Escalate**, follow the route it names.
83	
84	Ribbons tell you what you may share: **Client-facing: approved for sharing** or **Partner only: do not share**.
85	
86	### C01-L7 Getting help
87	
88	Use a meeting request in the portal. The types are joint sales, technical scoping, bespoke discovery, commercial assistance, proposal review, training and escalation. Give one to five preferred times and your time zone. ScaleSmiths confirms, proposes an alternative or asks for information. Nothing is booked until it is confirmed.
89	
90	Send: the business name, what they asked, what you have already said, and any deadline the client mentioned.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## C02 Professional Website Development
95	
96	### C02-L1 What a website project includes
97	
98	**Sources:** faq:website-included, faq:seo-in-build.
99	
100	A typical project covers agreed messaging, page structure, a responsive build, on-page search foundations (metadata, canonicals, structured data, headings, internal links, indexation controls, page speed) and a route from visitor to enquiry, plus launch support for that scope. **The proposal is the list of what is included.**
101	
102	### C02-L2 What is separate
103	
104	Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support are separate unless the proposal includes them. Managed Business Email is separate unless a combined arrangement is written in. This is not a trick; it is what keeps prices honest.
105	
106	**Say it like this:** "The build includes the search foundations. Ongoing SEO and support are separate, and the proposal spells out exactly what's in."
107	
108	### C02-L3 Price and proposal
109	
110	Website design and development starts **from £2,000**. A quote is calculated from requirements, the complexity of journeys and systems, and the deliverables written into the proposal. Never estimate a final price yourself. If a prospect pushes for a number, say the published starting price, explain the boundary and offer a proper quote or the Business Growth Audit.
111	
112	### C02-L4 Timelines
113	
114	**Source:** faq:timeline. Timing is confirmed after discovery because content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk change the schedule more than page count. The proposal records the range and its assumptions. **Do not give a timeline.**
115	
116	### C02-L5 Ownership and editing
117	
118	**Sources:** faq:website-ownership, faq:code-ownership, faq:self-editing.
119	
120	Ownership of the bespoke deliverable is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once agreed fees are paid. Clients keep their own materials, trademarks and data. ScaleSmiths keeps its pre-existing tools and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences.
121	
122	Self-editing is a scoping decision: an editable content layer is worth building when content changes often. Ask the client what they expect to change, and how often.
123	
124	### C02-L6 Technology and WordPress
125	
126	**Source:** faq:wordpress (*owner review flagged*). Published work is custom-built rather than WordPress themes. If a client runs WordPress, ScaleSmiths looks at what it does well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified. Never criticise a client's current platform or supplier.
127	
128	### C02-L7 Good-fit signals
129	
130	An established business with clear services; a site that no longer reflects the business; enquiries that matter commercially; evidence worth protecting; an owner willing to engage with discovery. Weaker fit: wants the cheapest possible page, wants guaranteed rankings, or cannot give time to review.
131	
132	### C02-L8 When it is not a standard website
133	
134	Route these to ScaleSmiths before saying anything about price: e-commerce (faq:ecommerce-builds: custom commerce only where its value justifies owning it), booking or quote workflows, customer portals, payments, integrations, migrations and anything with user accounts. Request **technical scoping**.
135	
136	---
137	
138	## C03 SEO and Digital Growth
139	
140	### C03-L1 What SEO is
141	
142	**Source:** faq:what-is-seo. SEO makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results. It has three parts: technical foundations that let search engines crawl and index pages, content that answers what people actually search for, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work, not a setting.
143	
144	### C03-L2 Local SEO
145	
146	**Source:** faq:what-is-local-seo. Local SEO targets people looking for a provider in a place. It depends on clear service and area descriptions, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.
147	
148	### C03-L3 Technical SEO
149	
150	**Source:** faq:technical-seo. Crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.
151	
152	### C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees
153	
154	**Sources:** faq:seo-timeline, faq:ranking-guarantees.
155	
156	Technical fixes can change indexation quickly. Content and authority work is measured over months. **No one can guarantee first place on Google**, because rankings depend on Google's systems, competitors and the searcher.
157	
158	**Say it like this:** "No honest agency can promise a position. What ScaleSmiths commits to is the work: technical health, content that matches real searches, credible proof, and measuring progress against a recorded baseline."
159	
160	### C03-L5 Build versus ongoing
161	
162	Search foundations are part of every build. Ongoing SEO (content, authority, measurement and iteration) is separate, scoped as a project or through a Growth Partnership.
163	
164	### C03-L6 SEO and paid search
165	
166	**Source:** faq:seo-and-google-ads. Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly. The right mix depends on urgency, margin and competition. ScaleSmiths will say when paid search is the more honest answer.
167	
168	### C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean
169	
170	**Sources:** service listing "SEO/AEO landing pages" (`web/src/lib/service-pages.ts`), `web/src/lib/agent-discovery.ts`. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-CNT-06`: no published FAQ answer covers AI search yet. This lesson is new wording.]*
171	
172	People increasingly ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) means making a site's content easy for those systems to understand and cite: pages that answer a buyer's real question directly, consistent facts, structured data and FAQ content, and clear service and location pages. ScaleSmiths builds pages this way and describes its own capabilities accurately in machine-readable form.
173	
174	What you must not say: that ScaleSmiths can get a business "into ChatGPT", guarantee being cited, or control what any AI system says. Those systems are run by third parties and change often.
175	
176	**Say it like this:** "Clear, well-structured answers help both search engines and AI assistants understand a business. Nobody can guarantee what an AI tool will say, but we can make sure your site gives it accurate, useful answers to work from."
177	
178	### C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google"
179	
180	**Source:** faq:not-on-google. The usual causes, in order: pages not indexed (robots rules, a noindex tag or a staging setting left on); indexed but not matching what people search for; or competing for terms far above the site's authority. Search Console usually separates these quickly, which is why the Business Growth Audit starts there.
181	
182	---
183	
184	## C04 Growth Partnerships
185	
186	### C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is
187	
188	**Sources:** `web/src/app/digital-growth-partnership/page.tsx`, faq:support-included.
189	
190	An ongoing partnership that can cover SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation and technical support, whether or not ScaleSmiths built the current site. The proposal defines priorities, working cadence, responsibilities and commercial terms.
191	
192	### C04-L2 What it is not
193	
194	It is not an unlimited marketing package, not just maintenance, and not a promise of results. Maintenance protects dependable operation; SEO, content, design changes and integrations are improvement work and are scoped as such.
195	
196	### C04-L3 Price and term
197	
198	The published price is **from £350 per month**. The proposal sets the final scope and price. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the draft programme models a twelve-month minimum term (`standard-v2`, disabled). Whether, and how, a minimum term is presented to clients is founder decision `AP-COM-03`. Until then, do not mention a term.]*
199	
200	### C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities
201	
202	**Source:** faq:request-priority. Work follows an agreed roadmap and a prioritised backlog, not a first-come queue. Incidents affecting a live service come first. Clients raise and track requests in the ScaleSmiths client portal.
203	
204	### C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring
205	
206	**Sources:** faq:hosting-included, faq:monitoring. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or a separate managed service; the order states what is covered. Monitoring is scoped to the actual stack. Business email is separate unless combined in writing.
207	
208	### C04-L6 After a build
209	
210	**Source:** faq:support. Launch is a measurement point, not the end. The production site is verified, measurement connected and ownership of accounts agreed. A Growth Partnership can then continue the work.
211	
212	### C04-L7 Existing websites
213	
214	**Source:** faq:manage-external-site. ScaleSmiths can often manage a site it did not build, after reviewing its code, hosting, access and update path. That review may identify prerequisite repairs, or show the platform needs its original specialist. It will not take on an unknown system blind.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## C05 Website Migration
219	
220	### C05-L1 Types of migration
221	
222	A platform rebuild (for example WordPress or Shopify to custom), a hosting move, a domain change, or a content-management change. Each has different risks. Many projects combine several.
223	
224	### C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves
225	
226	**Sources:** faq:website-migration, faq:rebuilds. ScaleSmiths reviews current code, licences, data, deployment and connected services first, then recommends a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration, whichever the evidence supports. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved onto self-hosted infrastructure.
227	
228	### C05-L3 Redirects and search risk
229	
230	**Source:** faq:seo-rebuild (*owner review flagged*). Any rebuild carries some search risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. Risk is reduced by mapping old URLs to new ones with redirects, carrying over content that performs, preserving metadata and structured data, and checking indexing after launch.
231	
232	### C05-L4 What to collect
233	
234	Who controls the domain and registrar; current hosting; access to the site's admin; Google Search Console and analytics access (if any); a list of integrations (forms, booking, payments, email marketing); any plugin or theme licences; and the business's deadline (for example a hosting contract ending).
235	
236	### C05-L5 Red flags
237	
238	Nobody knows who controls the domain; the domain is close to expiry; the previous supplier holds all access; unlicensed or abandoned plugins; data held only in the old platform; a hard deadline within weeks. None of these is a reason to walk away, but every one is a reason to escalate early.
239	
240	### C05-L6 Escalation
241	
242	Every migration goes to **technical scoping** before any price or timeline is discussed. Share what you collected in C05-L4.
243	
244	---
245	
246	## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation
247	
248	### C06-L1 Custom versus off the shelf
249	
250	**Source:** faq:custom-software. Custom software is justified when the workflow genuinely differentiates the business, when existing tools create material friction, or when integration and data-ownership needs cannot be met by configuration. If a proven product already fits, buying and integrating it is usually better, and ScaleSmiths will say so.
251	
252	### C06-L2 What we have built
253	
254	**Sources:** faq:crm (*owner review flagged*), faq:customer-portals, faq:stripe, faq:integrations, faq:internal-admin-systems.
255	
256	Published examples, described as the FAQ library describes them:
257	
258	- a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM for Confirm-A-Kill (enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits);
259	- a quote management admin behind the CSDS website;
260	- Stripe subscription billing for The Business Circle; plans, seats and credits for Prymal;
261	- booking integration and review aggregation for Glow Tanning;
262	- product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints;
263	- member and admin applications for VeteranFinder;
264	- ScaleSmiths' own client portal, with tenant isolation enforced on the server.
265	
266	Describe what was built. Do not quote outcomes, figures or client opinions unless an approved resource contains them (`AP-PROOF-01`).
267	
268	### C06-L3 Automating a workflow
269	
270	**Source:** faq:process-automation. Start with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and useful outcome can be defined. Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make; high-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record.
271	
272	### C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes
273	
274	**Source:** faq:replace-spreadsheets. Replace gradually, beginning with the highest-friction workflow. Rebuilding everything at once is the common failure.
275	
276	### C06-L5 AI, honestly
277	
278	Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than a language model. AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required. Do not sell "AI" as a feature in itself.
279	
280	### C06-L6 Phases and scoping
281	
282	**Sources:** faq:phases, faq:software-scaling, `engagement-models.ts`. Custom work is scoped after discovery and never priced against a website starting price. The first release has a defined boundary; later phases extend a system that is understood.
283	
284	### C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests
285	
286	Request a **bespoke discovery** meeting when the client describes a workflow, system or integration rather than a website. Include: the workflow in the client's words, the people involved, current tools, rough volumes, what goes wrong today, and any deadline. *[PROPOSED POLICY: bespoke commission eligibility and existing-customer attribution are open founder decisions.]*
287

| Offer | Published price |
|---|---|
| Website design and development | From £2,000 |
| Growth Partnership | From £350 per month |
| Business Growth Audit | £395 |
| Managed Business Email | From £15 per month (three 5GB mailboxes, setup included) |

It also takes on established-business transformation and custom platforms. These are **never** sold against a website starting price and are scoped after discovery.

A starting price is exactly that. The published boundary reads: "A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed result." Prices are in GBP only. ScaleSmiths does not bill in other currencies or publish converted prices.

**Rule:** quote only these four figures, always with the boundary. Anything else is a ScaleSmiths proposal.

### C01-L3 How we work

**Sources:** faq:after-enquiry, faq:timeline, faq:phases, faq:improvement-measurement.

1. **Enquiry.** The founders review what is sent and reply with a sensible next step: questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal. Sending a form takes no payment and creates no contract.
2. **Discovery.** What the business sells, who buys, how they choose, what the current site does well, and what evidence exists.
3. **Written proposal.** Scope, deliverables, delivery range and assumptions, and payment terms.
4. **Phased delivery.** A dependable first release; later work follows evidence.
5. **Measurement.** Agreed signals, reviewed in conversation, not invented targets.

### C01-L4 What an independent partner does

**Sources:** `/partners` page copy (`web/src/app/partners/page.tsx`, draft, not approved), [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).

As an independent partner you introduce suitable businesses, have early conversations, register prospects in the Partner Portal and support the relationship. ScaleSmiths scopes, prices, contracts and delivers the work.

You decide how, when and whether you work. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the final partner agreement defines the relationship. This lesson must be checked against it.]*

You do **not**: issue quotes, agree discounts, promise timelines, sign anything on ScaleSmiths' behalf, or handle client payments.

### C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned

**Sources:** `FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`.

The programme uses four labels: **Available subject to approval**, **Planned**, **In development** and **Not available in this market**. Read them literally:

- *Available subject to approval* means designed but dependent on the final agreement and approvals.
- *Planned* means not built or not operational, with no date.
- *In development* means being built, not yet available.

In the portal, content carries its own status: only approved, published items are shown, each with a version and review date. If you remember something from a conversation that is not in an approved item, it is not policy.

### C01-L6 Finding answers fast

Start with knowledge search. Type the question as the client asked it ("do you do hosting?"). Results show approved answers with three parts: the precise answer for you, a client-friendly explanation you may use, and the limitation. If an entry says **Escalate**, follow the route it names.

Ribbons tell you what you may share: **Client-facing: approved for sharing** or **Partner only: do not share**.

### C01-L7 Getting help

Use a meeting request in the portal. The types are joint sales, technical scoping, bespoke discovery, commercial assistance, proposal review, training and escalation. Give one to five preferred times and your time zone. ScaleSmiths confirms, proposes an alternative or asks for information. Nothing is booked until it is confirmed.

Send: the business name, what they asked, what you have already said, and any deadline the client mentioned.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

### C02-L1 What a website project includes

**Sources:** faq:website-included, faq:seo-in-build.

A typical project covers agreed messaging, page structure, a responsive build, on-page search foundations (metadata, canonicals, structured data, headings, internal links, indexation controls, page speed) and a route from visitor to enquiry, plus launch support for that scope. **The proposal is the list of what is included.**

### C02-L2 What is separate

Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support are separate unless the proposal includes them. Managed Business Email is separate unless a combined arrangement is written in. This is not a trick; it is what keeps prices honest.

**Say it like this:** "The build includes the search foundations. Ongoing SEO and support are separate, and the proposal spells out exactly what's in."

### C02-L3 Price and proposal

Website design and development starts **from £2,000**. A quote is calculated from requirements, the complexity of journeys and systems, and the deliverables written into the proposal. Never estimate a final price yourself. If a prospect pushes for a number, say the published starting price, explain the boundary and offer a proper quote or the Business Growth Audit.

### C02-L4 Timelines

**Source:** faq:timeline. Timing is confirmed after discovery because content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk change the schedule more than page count. The proposal records the range and its assumptions. **Do not give a timeline.**

### C02-L5 Ownership and editing

**Sources:** faq:website-ownership, faq:code-ownership, faq:self-editing.

Ownership of the bespoke deliverable is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once agreed fees are paid. Clients keep their own materials, trademarks and data. ScaleSmiths keeps its pre-existing tools and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences.

Self-editing is a scoping decision: an editable content layer is worth building when content changes often. Ask the client what they expect to change, and how often.

### C02-L6 Technology and WordPress

**Source:** faq:wordpress (*owner review flagged*). Published work is custom-built rather than WordPress themes. If a client runs WordPress, ScaleSmiths looks at what it does well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified. Never criticise a client's current platform or supplier.

### C02-L7 Good-fit signals

An established business with clear services; a site that no longer reflects the business; enquiries that matter commercially; evidence worth protecting; an owner willing to engage with discovery. Weaker fit: wants the cheapest possible page, wants guaranteed rankings, or cannot give time to review.

### C02-L8 When it is not a standard website

Route these to ScaleSmiths before saying anything about price: e-commerce (faq:ecommerce-builds: custom commerce only where its value justifies owning it), booking or quote workflows, customer portals, payments, integrations, migrations and anything with user accounts. Request **technical scoping**.

---

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

### C03-L1 What SEO is

**Source:** faq:what-is-seo. SEO makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results. It has three parts: technical foundations that let search engines crawl and index pages, content that answers what people actually search for, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work, not a setting.

### C03-L2 Local SEO

**Source:** faq:what-is-local-seo. Local SEO targets people looking for a provider in a place. It depends on clear service and area descriptions, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.

### C03-L3 Technical SEO

**Source:** faq:technical-seo. Crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.

### C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees

**Sources:** faq:seo-timeline, faq:ranking-guarantees.

Technical fixes can change indexation quickly. Content and authority work is measured over months. **No one can guarantee first place on Google**, because rankings depend on Google's systems, competitors and the searcher.

**Say it like this:** "No honest agency can promise a position. What ScaleSmiths commits to is the work: technical health, content that matches real searches, credible proof, and measuring progress against a recorded baseline."

### C03-L5 Build versus ongoing

Search foundations are part of every build. Ongoing SEO (content, authority, measurement and iteration) is separate, scoped as a project or through a Growth Partnership.

### C03-L6 SEO and paid search

**Source:** faq:seo-and-google-ads. Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly. The right mix depends on urgency, margin and competition. ScaleSmiths will say when paid search is the more honest answer.

### C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean

**Sources:** service listing "SEO/AEO landing pages" (`web/src/lib/service-pages.ts`), `web/src/lib/agent-discovery.ts`. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-CNT-06`: no published FAQ answer covers AI search yet. This lesson is new wording.]*

People increasingly ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) means making a site's content easy for those systems to understand and cite: pages that answer a buyer's real question directly, consistent facts, structured data and FAQ content, and clear service and location pages. ScaleSmiths builds pages this way and describes its own capabilities accurately in machine-readable form.

What you must not say: that ScaleSmiths can get a business "into ChatGPT", guarantee being cited, or control what any AI system says. Those systems are run by third parties and change often.

**Say it like this:** "Clear, well-structured answers help both search engines and AI assistants understand a business. Nobody can guarantee what an AI tool will say, but we can make sure your site gives it accurate, useful answers to work from."

### C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google"

**Source:** faq:not-on-google. The usual causes, in order: pages not indexed (robots rules, a noindex tag or a staging setting left on); indexed but not matching what people search for; or competing for terms far above the site's authority. Search Console usually separates these quickly, which is why the Business Growth Audit starts there.

---

## C04 Growth Partnerships

### C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is

**Sources:** `web/src/app/digital-growth-partnership/page.tsx`, faq:support-included.

An ongoing partnership that can cover SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation and technical support, whether or not ScaleSmiths built the current site. The proposal defines priorities, working cadence, responsibilities and commercial terms.

### C04-L2 What it is not

It is not an unlimited marketing package, not just maintenance, and not a promise of results. Maintenance protects dependable operation; SEO, content, design changes and integrations are improvement work and are scoped as such.

### C04-L3 Price and term

The published price is **from £350 per month**. The proposal sets the final scope and price. *[PROPOSED POLICY: the draft programme models a twelve-month minimum term (`standard-v2`, disabled). Whether, and how, a minimum term is presented to clients is founder decision `AP-COM-03`. Until then, do not mention a term.]*

### C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities

**Source:** faq:request-priority. Work follows an agreed roadmap and a prioritised backlog, not a first-come queue. Incidents affecting a live service come first. Clients raise and track requests in the ScaleSmiths client portal.

### C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring

**Sources:** faq:hosting-included, faq:monitoring. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or a separate managed service; the order states what is covered. Monitoring is scoped to the actual stack. Business email is separate unless combined in writing.

### C04-L6 After a build

**Source:** faq:support. Launch is a measurement point, not the end. The production site is verified, measurement connected and ownership of accounts agreed. A Growth Partnership can then continue the work.

### C04-L7 Existing websites

**Source:** faq:manage-external-site. ScaleSmiths can often manage a site it did not build, after reviewing its code, hosting, access and update path. That review may identify prerequisite repairs, or show the platform needs its original specialist. It will not take on an unknown system blind.

---

## C05 Website Migration

### C05-L1 Types of migration

A platform rebuild (for example WordPress or Shopify to custom), a hosting move, a domain change, or a content-management change. Each has different risks. Many projects combine several.

### C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves

**Sources:** faq:website-migration, faq:rebuilds. ScaleSmiths reviews current code, licences, data, deployment and connected services first, then recommends a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration, whichever the evidence supports. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved onto self-hosted infrastructure.

### C05-L3 Redirects and search risk

**Source:** faq:seo-rebuild (*owner review flagged*). Any rebuild carries some search risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. Risk is reduced by mapping old URLs to new ones with redirects, carrying over content that performs, preserving metadata and structured data, and checking indexing after launch.

### C05-L4 What to collect

Who controls the domain and registrar; current hosting; access to the site's admin; Google Search Console and analytics access (if any); a list of integrations (forms, booking, payments, email marketing); any plugin or theme licences; and the business's deadline (for example a hosting contract ending).

### C05-L5 Red flags

Nobody knows who controls the domain; the domain is close to expiry; the previous supplier holds all access; unlicensed or abandoned plugins; data held only in the old platform; a hard deadline within weeks. None of these is a reason to walk away, but every one is a reason to escalate early.

### C05-L6 Escalation

Every migration goes to **technical scoping** before any price or timeline is discussed. Share what you collected in C05-L4.

---

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

### C06-L1 Custom versus off the shelf

**Source:** faq:custom-software. Custom software is justified when the workflow genuinely differentiates the business, when existing tools create material friction, or when integration and data-ownership needs cannot be met by configuration. If a proven product already fits, buying and integrating it is usually better, and ScaleSmiths will say so.

### C06-L2 What we have built

**Sources:** faq:crm (*owner review flagged*), faq:customer-portals, faq:stripe, faq:integrations, faq:internal-admin-systems.

Published examples, described as the FAQ library describes them:

- a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM for Confirm-A-Kill (enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits);
- a quote management admin behind the CSDS website;
- Stripe subscription billing for The Business Circle; plans, seats and credits for Prymal;
- booking integration and review aggregation for Glow Tanning;
- product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints;
- member and admin applications for VeteranFinder;
- ScaleSmiths' own client portal, with tenant isolation enforced on the server.

Describe what was built. Do not quote outcomes, figures or client opinions unless an approved resource contains them (`AP-PROOF-01`).

### C06-L3 Automating a workflow

**Source:** faq:process-automation. Start with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and useful outcome can be defined. Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make; high-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record.

### C06-L4 Spreadsheets and manual processes

**Source:** faq:replace-spreadsheets. Replace gradually, beginning with the highest-friction workflow. Rebuilding everything at once is the common failure.

### C06-L5 AI, honestly

Deterministic rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than a language model. AI is used where interpretation is genuinely required. Do not sell "AI" as a feature in itself.

### C06-L6 Phases and scoping

**Sources:** faq:phases, faq:software-scaling, `engagement-models.ts`. Custom work is scoped after discovery and never priced against a website starting price. The first release has a defined boundary; later phases extend a system that is understood.

### C06-L7 Bespoke discovery requests

Request a **bespoke discovery** meeting when the client describes a workflow, system or integration rather than a website. Include: the workflow in the client's words, the people involved, current tools, rough volumes, what goes wrong today, and any deadline. *[PROPOSED POLICY: bespoke commission eligibility and existing-customer attribution are open founder decisions.]*

1	# Initial lesson content: courses 7 to 13
2	
3	**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published, not for use with partners or clients.** Courses C07, C11 and C12 are also `BLOCKED` on founder, legal and accounting decisions; see [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md). Conventions are as in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## C07 Finding Prospects (BLOCKED: marketing process)
8	
9	### C07-L1 Good-fit businesses
10	
11	Look for established businesses with a clear offer and customers who search before they buy: trades, professional services, health and clinics, local retail, specialist manufacturers. Signals: an outdated or slow site, weak mobile experience, no clear route to enquire, services missing from the site, or an owner who talks about growth. Weaker fit: no budget at all, wants a template, or wants a guarantee.
12	
13	### C07-L2 Warm introductions
14	
15	Your own professional network is the best starting point. Introduce people who would genuinely benefit, ask before passing on anyone's details, and be open that you are an independent partner of ScaleSmiths.
16	
17	### C07-L3 Registering a prospect
18	
19	Register a prospect in the Partner Portal before detailed conversations. Registration is a preliminary record: duplicates and existing clients are checked, and lead protection applies to ordinary registrations. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-COM-06`: the lead protection term, expiry and dispute process are not approved. Do not tell a partner or prospect how long protection lasts.]*
20	
21	### C07-L4 Researched prospects
22	
23	*[PROPOSED POLICY]* ScaleSmiths may allocate researched businesses, subject to availability, screening and market approval. No fixed number is guaranteed and nothing is contacted by ScaleSmiths on your behalf. Treat each allocated business as **not assessed for outreach** until the approved process says otherwise.
24	
25	### C07-L5 Contact rules
26	
27	*[BLOCKED: approved marketing process, `AP-LEG-03`]* Direct marketing is regulated. For UK business-to-business marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check the TPS and CTPS registers and their own do-not-call lists, and electronic marketing rules vary by channel and subscriber type ([ICO guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)). Until ScaleSmiths approves a process, **do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf.**
28	
29	### C07-L6 Suppression and objections
30	
31	If someone asks not to be contacted, stop, record it in the portal and tell ScaleSmiths. Never argue with an opt-out or try another channel.
32	
33	### C07-L7 Sectors and exclusivity
34	
35	Some clients may have sector exclusivity. If the portal shows "commercial checks in progress", that is all you will be told. The details are confidential and decided by founders. Do not guess or ask the prospect about competitors.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## C08 Discovery Meetings
40	
41	### C08-L1 Preparing
42	
43	Spend fifteen minutes before the meeting: read their website on a phone, search for their main service and town, note whether they appear, check whether they have a Google Business Profile, and read any reviews. Use [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md). Note questions, not conclusions.
44	
45	### C08-L2 Setting the agenda
46	
47	Open with purpose and time: "I'd like to understand how the business wins customers today and where the website helps or gets in the way. Then, if it makes sense, I'll explain how ScaleSmiths could help and what the next step would be." Confirm how long they have.
48	
49	### C08-L3 The core questions
50	
51	Use [R07 Discovery questionnaire](resources/R07-discovery-questionnaire.md). The essentials:
52	
53	1. What do you sell, and which services matter most commercially?
54	2. Who are your best customers and how do they find you?
55	3. What does your current website do well? What frustrates you?
56	4. What evidence do you have: enquiries, calls, analytics, Search Console?
57	5. What systems do you use (booking, CRM, email, payments)?
58	6. Who controls the domain, hosting and website accounts?
59	7. What would a good result look like in a year?
60	8. Is there a deadline or trigger?
61	9. Have you set aside a budget range?
62	
63	### C08-L4 Listening for fit
64	
65	- "We look dated / we don't get enquiries from the site" → website project.
66	- "We have a decent site but nobody finds it" → Business Growth Audit or Growth Partnership.
67	- "We're not sure what's wrong" → Business Growth Audit.
68	- "We run everything on spreadsheets / our booking is a mess" → bespoke discovery.
69	- "Our emails go to spam / we use a Gmail address" → Managed Business Email.
70	
71	### C08-L5 What not to say
72	
73	No prices beyond the four published starting prices. No timelines. No rankings, traffic or revenue predictions. No commitments about what is included. No criticism of their current supplier. No mention of your commission.
74	
75	### C08-L6 Writing up
76	
77	Write notes the same day in the questionnaire format: facts they told you, your observations (clearly marked as yours), open questions and the agreed next step.
78	
79	### C08-L7 Next steps
80	
81	Offer one clear next step: a quote request, the Business Growth Audit (£395), a joint sales meeting, or technical scoping. Confirm it in writing using [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).
82	
83	---
84	
85	## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths
86	
87	### C09-L1 Problem first
88	
89	Open by playing back what you heard: "You said most new customers come from referrals, and the site doesn't explain your commercial services." Then connect each part of your presentation to one of those points.
90	
91	### C09-L2 The ScaleSmiths approach
92	
93	Four points, each from published wording: protect what already works; write the scope down; deliver in phases with a dependable first release; measure against agreed signals instead of invented targets.
94	
95	### C09-L3 Using published work
96	
97	You may describe what was built for published clients as the FAQ library and case studies describe it (see C06-L2), once founders approve partner use (`AP-PROOF-01`). Point people to the case studies on the ScaleSmiths website instead of retelling them.
98	
99	### C09-L4 Proof you must not use
100	
101	Testimonials or quotes not shown on the site; outcome figures that are not in an approved resource; client names that are not published; "we've helped hundreds of businesses"-style claims; screenshots of private systems.
102	
103	### C09-L5 Presenting price
104	
105	State the relevant published starting price and the boundary. Suggest the Business Growth Audit where the need is unclear: it is a one-time review and prioritised roadmap, and where the published terms apply the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.
106	
107	### C09-L6 A respectful close
108	
109	"Would it help if I arranged a proper quote?" is enough. Agree a date to follow up. Never use false urgency ("this price ends Friday").
110	
111	---
112	
113	## C10 Objection Handling
114	
115	The full set of responses, with approval status for each, is in [R08 Objection-handling playbook](resources/R08-objection-handling-playbook.md).
116	
117	### C10-L1 The pattern
118	
119	1. **Acknowledge** the concern without arguing.
120	2. **Clarify** what is behind it with a question.
121	3. **Answer** with approved wording.
122	4. **Confirm** whether that helps, and agree the next step.
123	
124	### C10-L2 When to stop
125	
126	Stop if the business is not a good fit, if the person is under pressure or vulnerable, or if the objection needs ScaleSmiths (contract terms, technical risk, a complaint about a previous supplier, a legal question). Saying "that's a question for ScaleSmiths; I'll get you a proper answer" is a good outcome.
127	
128	### C10-L3 "It is too expensive"
129	
130	Clarify: compared with what, and for what scope? Explain that a starting price is an entry point for an agreed scope, that proposals list what is included, that work can be phased, and that the Business Growth Audit is a lower-cost first step. **Never offer a discount.** Discount allowances are disabled and only founders can reserve one *[PROPOSED POLICY]*.
131	
132	### C10-L4 "We already have a website or an agency"
133	
134	Respect the existing relationship. ScaleSmiths starts by reviewing what currently works. An audit can serve as an independent second opinion, and its findings are useful whoever implements them.
135	
136	### C10-L5 "Can you guarantee results?"
137	
138	No. Use the approved line from C03-L4. Explain that commitments are to the work and to measuring against a baseline.
139	
140	### C10-L6 "We use WordPress, Wix or Shopify"
141	
142	ScaleSmiths is not anti-platform. It looks at what the current platform is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified, and where an established platform fits, configuring it may be the better decision.
143	
144	### C10-L7 "We need to think about it"
145	
146	Agree, summarise what you discussed, offer to send a short written summary, and agree when to follow up.
147	
148	### C10-L8 Using the objection workspace
149	
150	Search for the objection in the client's words, read the partner guidance, then copy only the **client-facing** line. Practise responses aloud. Report new objections to ScaleSmiths so an approved answer can be written.
151	
152	---
153	
154	## C11 Commercial Policies (BLOCKED: agreement and terms)
155	
156	> Every partner-term figure in this course is **PROPOSED POLICY**: an illustration of the proposed programme, not an approved agreement. Plans are disabled by default. No reward is payable. This course must not be published until the decisions listed in [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) are recorded.
157	
158	### C11-L1 Published starting prices
159	
160	Website from £2,000; Growth Partnership from £350 per month; Business Growth Audit £395; business email from £15 per month. GBP, and always with the starting-price boundary.
161	
162	### C11-L2 Proposals and payment terms
163	
164	**Source:** faq:deposit. Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set in each proposal and signed order. There is no blanket published deposit policy. Never describe a payment schedule to a client.
165	
166	### C11-L3 How commission is proposed to work
167	
168	*[PROPOSED POLICY]* Source: `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../COMMISSION-RULES.md).
169	
170	- Commission is proposed at **30% of eligible payments actually collected**, VAT-exclusive, under the final partner agreement.

# Initial lesson content: courses 7 to 13

**Status: DRAFT. Not approved, not published, not for use with partners or clients.** Courses C07, C11 and C12 are also `BLOCKED` on founder, legal and accounting decisions; see [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md). Conventions are as in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md).

---

## C07 Finding Prospects (BLOCKED: marketing process)

### C07-L1 Good-fit businesses

Look for established businesses with a clear offer and customers who search before they buy: trades, professional services, health and clinics, local retail, specialist manufacturers. Signals: an outdated or slow site, weak mobile experience, no clear route to enquire, services missing from the site, or an owner who talks about growth. Weaker fit: no budget at all, wants a template, or wants a guarantee.

### C07-L2 Warm introductions

Your own professional network is the best starting point. Introduce people who would genuinely benefit, ask before passing on anyone's details, and be open that you are an independent partner of ScaleSmiths.

### C07-L3 Registering a prospect

Register a prospect in the Partner Portal before detailed conversations. Registration is a preliminary record: duplicates and existing clients are checked, and lead protection applies to ordinary registrations. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-COM-06`: the lead protection term, expiry and dispute process are not approved. Do not tell a partner or prospect how long protection lasts.]*

### C07-L4 Researched prospects

*[PROPOSED POLICY]* ScaleSmiths may allocate researched businesses, subject to availability, screening and market approval. No fixed number is guaranteed and nothing is contacted by ScaleSmiths on your behalf. Treat each allocated business as **not assessed for outreach** until the approved process says otherwise.

### C07-L5 Contact rules

*[BLOCKED: approved marketing process, `AP-LEG-03`]* Direct marketing is regulated. For UK business-to-business marketing calls, the ICO directs organisations to check the TPS and CTPS registers and their own do-not-call lists, and electronic marketing rules vary by channel and subscriber type ([ICO guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)). Until ScaleSmiths approves a process, **do not make unsolicited calls or send unsolicited marketing emails on ScaleSmiths' behalf.**

### C07-L6 Suppression and objections

If someone asks not to be contacted, stop, record it in the portal and tell ScaleSmiths. Never argue with an opt-out or try another channel.

### C07-L7 Sectors and exclusivity

Some clients may have sector exclusivity. If the portal shows "commercial checks in progress", that is all you will be told. The details are confidential and decided by founders. Do not guess or ask the prospect about competitors.

---

## C08 Discovery Meetings

### C08-L1 Preparing

Spend fifteen minutes before the meeting: read their website on a phone, search for their main service and town, note whether they appear, check whether they have a Google Business Profile, and read any reviews. Use [R09 Meeting preparation checklist](resources/R09-meeting-preparation-checklist.md). Note questions, not conclusions.

### C08-L2 Setting the agenda

Open with purpose and time: "I'd like to understand how the business wins customers today and where the website helps or gets in the way. Then, if it makes sense, I'll explain how ScaleSmiths could help and what the next step would be." Confirm how long they have.

### C08-L3 The core questions

Use [R07 Discovery questionnaire](resources/R07-discovery-questionnaire.md). The essentials:

1. What do you sell, and which services matter most commercially?
2. Who are your best customers and how do they find you?
3. What does your current website do well? What frustrates you?
4. What evidence do you have: enquiries, calls, analytics, Search Console?
5. What systems do you use (booking, CRM, email, payments)?
6. Who controls the domain, hosting and website accounts?
7. What would a good result look like in a year?
8. Is there a deadline or trigger?
9. Have you set aside a budget range?

### C08-L4 Listening for fit

- "We look dated / we don't get enquiries from the site" → website project.
- "We have a decent site but nobody finds it" → Business Growth Audit or Growth Partnership.
- "We're not sure what's wrong" → Business Growth Audit.
- "We run everything on spreadsheets / our booking is a mess" → bespoke discovery.
- "Our emails go to spam / we use a Gmail address" → Managed Business Email.

### C08-L5 What not to say

No prices beyond the four published starting prices. No timelines. No rankings, traffic or revenue predictions. No commitments about what is included. No criticism of their current supplier. No mention of your commission.

### C08-L6 Writing up

Write notes the same day in the questionnaire format: facts they told you, your observations (clearly marked as yours), open questions and the agreed next step.

### C08-L7 Next steps

Offer one clear next step: a quote request, the Business Growth Audit (£395), a joint sales meeting, or technical scoping. Confirm it in writing using [R13 Follow-up templates](resources/R13-follow-up-templates.md).

---

## C09 Presenting ScaleSmiths

### C09-L1 Problem first

Open by playing back what you heard: "You said most new customers come from referrals, and the site doesn't explain your commercial services." Then connect each part of your presentation to one of those points.

### C09-L2 The ScaleSmiths approach

Four points, each from published wording: protect what already works; write the scope down; deliver in phases with a dependable first release; measure against agreed signals instead of invented targets.

### C09-L3 Using published work

You may describe what was built for published clients as the FAQ library and case studies describe it (see C06-L2), once founders approve partner use (`AP-PROOF-01`). Point people to the case studies on the ScaleSmiths website instead of retelling them.

### C09-L4 Proof you must not use

Testimonials or quotes not shown on the site; outcome figures that are not in an approved resource; client names that are not published; "we've helped hundreds of businesses"-style claims; screenshots of private systems.

### C09-L5 Presenting price

State the relevant published starting price and the boundary. Suggest the Business Growth Audit where the need is unclear: it is a one-time review and prioritised roadmap, and where the published terms apply the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.

### C09-L6 A respectful close

"Would it help if I arranged a proper quote?" is enough. Agree a date to follow up. Never use false urgency ("this price ends Friday").

---

## C10 Objection Handling

The full set of responses, with approval status for each, is in [R08 Objection-handling playbook](resources/R08-objection-handling-playbook.md).

### C10-L1 The pattern

1. **Acknowledge** the concern without arguing.
2. **Clarify** what is behind it with a question.
3. **Answer** with approved wording.
4. **Confirm** whether that helps, and agree the next step.

### C10-L2 When to stop

Stop if the business is not a good fit, if the person is under pressure or vulnerable, or if the objection needs ScaleSmiths (contract terms, technical risk, a complaint about a previous supplier, a legal question). Saying "that's a question for ScaleSmiths; I'll get you a proper answer" is a good outcome.

### C10-L3 "It is too expensive"

Clarify: compared with what, and for what scope? Explain that a starting price is an entry point for an agreed scope, that proposals list what is included, that work can be phased, and that the Business Growth Audit is a lower-cost first step. **Never offer a discount.** Discount allowances are disabled and only founders can reserve one *[PROPOSED POLICY]*.

### C10-L4 "We already have a website or an agency"

Respect the existing relationship. ScaleSmiths starts by reviewing what currently works. An audit can serve as an independent second opinion, and its findings are useful whoever implements them.

### C10-L5 "Can you guarantee results?"

No. Use the approved line from C03-L4. Explain that commitments are to the work and to measuring against a baseline.

### C10-L6 "We use WordPress, Wix or Shopify"

ScaleSmiths is not anti-platform. It looks at what the current platform is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified, and where an established platform fits, configuring it may be the better decision.

### C10-L7 "We need to think about it"

Agree, summarise what you discussed, offer to send a short written summary, and agree when to follow up.

### C10-L8 Using the objection workspace

Search for the objection in the client's words, read the partner guidance, then copy only the **client-facing** line. Practise responses aloud. Report new objections to ScaleSmiths so an approved answer can be written.

---

**Source:** faq:deposit. Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set in each proposal and signed order. There is no blanket published deposit policy. Never describe a payment schedule to a client.

*[PROPOSED POLICY]* Source: `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../COMMISSION-RULES.md).

1	# Knowledge base: approved-content architecture and article inventory
2	
3	**Status: DRAFT. No entry is approved or published.** Entries restate published wording where it exists; the approval status says which. Engineering design (data model, search, lifecycle) is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).
4	
5	## 1. How the knowledge base works
6	
7	**Purpose:** give partners a precise, approved answer to the questions prospects actually ask, with a line they may say to the client, the limit of that answer, and when to hand over.
8	
9	**Required fields for every entry** (the service refuses review without them):
10	
11	| Field | Meaning |
12	|---|---|
13	| Question | As a client would ask it, plus aliases |
14	| Answer | Precise partner-facing answer |
15	| Client-friendly explanation | Wording a partner may say or send. Contains no partner-only information |
16	| Source | Repository file and key, or an approved founder document. No source, no entry |
17	| Limitation | What the answer does not cover or must not be stretched to mean |
18	| Escalation | `always`, `when <condition>`, or `never`, with the meeting type |
19	| Approval status | One of the package statuses; later, the recorded approval with reviewer and review-by date |
20	
21	**Source hierarchy** (highest first): signed agreement or founder decision record → published site source (`published-starting-prices.ts`, `faq-library.ts`, `legal-policies.ts`) → B0 system behaviour → this package's drafts.
22	
23	**Search approach:** deterministic PostgreSQL full-text search over question, aliases, answer and topic, with a founder-managed synonym list, exact alias matching first and stable ordering. No language model, no embeddings. Only published, in-review-window entries for the caller's audience are searchable. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 4.
24	
25	**Review cadence (proposed, `AP-GOV-06`):** commercial entries every 3 months; service entries every 6 months; any entry immediately when its source file changes. A CI check that flags entries whose source key changed is a Phase 3 candidate.
26	
27	**Topic taxonomy:** hosting, domains, DNS, business email, website security, analytics, SEO, AI search, WordPress migration, redirects, accessibility, e-commerce, booking systems, CRM, custom software, automation, commercial terms, payment schedules, commission, client onboarding.
28	
29	## 2. Article inventory
30	
31	`faq:<key>` refers to `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`. Status `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` applies to the published *wording*; the knowledge entry as a whole remains `DRAFT` until approved.
32	
33	### Hosting
34	
35	**KB-HOST-01 Do you provide hosting?**
36	- Answer: Yes. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx on a VPS and on managed platforms such as Vercel, chosen around the workload and support model. Hosting can be part of a build or a standalone managed service.
37	- Client explanation: "Yes. ScaleSmiths can host your site as part of the build or as a managed service, and they'll document exactly what's covered."
38	- Source: faq:hosting-provided, faq:hosting-location.
39	- Limitation: no published hosting price, uptime figure or provider list. Do not quote any.
40	- Escalation: when the client needs a price, a specific provider or a migration → `technical_scoping`.
41	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` wording; entry `DRAFT`.
42	
43	**KB-HOST-02 Is hosting included in a Growth Partnership?**
44	- Answer: Not automatically. It can be part of a Growth Partnership or a separate managed service; the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered.
45	- Client explanation: "It can be. Your agreement will list exactly what's covered."
46	- Source: faq:hosting-included.
47	- Limitation: do not imply hosting is bundled.
48	- Escalation: never.
49	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; entry `DRAFT`.
50	
51	**KB-HOST-03 Are websites backed up?**
52	- Answer: Backups are part of a managed hosting or maintenance arrangement, and the order states coverage and retention. They reduce risk but do not make loss impossible, and the online terms create no restoration guarantee, recovery point or recovery time.
53	- Client explanation: "Backups are part of managed hosting, and the agreement says exactly what's covered."
54	- Source: faq:backups.
55	- Limitation: no recovery-time or recovery-point promise.
56	- Escalation: when the client has lost data now → `escalation`.
57	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; entry `DRAFT`.
58	
59	### Domains and DNS
60	
61	**KB-DOM-01 Do you manage domains? Do we have to transfer ours?**
62	- Answer: The client remains the registrant unless a transfer is agreed in writing. ScaleSmiths needs appropriate access to configure records; a transfer is not automatically required. Registration or renewal administration is scoped explicitly if wanted.
63	- Client explanation: "You keep your domain. ScaleSmiths just needs the right access to set it up."
64	- Source: faq:domains.
65	- Limitation: never ask for registrar passwords.
66	- Escalation: when nobody knows who controls the domain, or it is close to expiry → `technical_scoping`.
67	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; entry `DRAFT`.
68	
69	**KB-DNS-01 Do you manage DNS?**
70	- Answer: Yes, where given appropriate access. Email onboarding includes the required mail and authentication records; website and hosting work includes the DNS changes a launch or migration needs. Delegated or scoped access is used where supported, and registrar passwords are never requested through a public form.
71	- Client explanation: "Yes. ScaleSmiths handles the DNS changes needed, using delegated access rather than your passwords."
72	- Source: faq:dns.
73	- Limitation: DNS for unrelated third-party services is not implied.
74	- Escalation: when DNS is broken now → `escalation`.
75	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; entry `DRAFT`.
76	
77	### Business email
78	
79	**KB-EMAIL-01 Do you provide business email?**
80	- Answer: Managed Business Email starts at £15 per month for three custom-domain mailboxes with 5GB each; initial mailbox and DNS setup is included. Webmail, desktop and mobile compatibility, aliases and forwarding, spam filtering, TLS transport, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Available standalone.
81	- Client explanation: "Yes, from £15 a month for three mailboxes on your own domain, with setup included."
82	- Source: faq:business-email, `published-starting-prices.ts`, `managed-business-email.ts`.
83	- Limitation: extra mailboxes are not included unless agreed.
84	- Escalation: when migrating existing mailboxes → `technical_scoping`.
85	- Status: `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; entry `DRAFT`.

## 1. How the knowledge base works

**Purpose:** give partners a precise, approved answer to the questions prospects actually ask, with a line they may say to the client, the limit of that answer, and when to hand over.

**Required fields for every entry** (the service refuses review without them):

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Question | As a client would ask it, plus aliases |
| Answer | Precise partner-facing answer |
| Client-friendly explanation | Wording a partner may say or send. Contains no partner-only information |
| Source | Repository file and key, or an approved founder document. No source, no entry |
| Limitation | What the answer does not cover or must not be stretched to mean |
| Escalation | `always`, `when <condition>`, or `never`, with the meeting type |
| Approval status | One of the package statuses; later, the recorded approval with reviewer and review-by date |

**Source hierarchy** (highest first): signed agreement or founder decision record → published site source (`published-starting-prices.ts`, `faq-library.ts`, `legal-policies.ts`) → B0 system behaviour → this package's drafts.

**Search approach:** deterministic PostgreSQL full-text search over question, aliases, answer and topic, with a founder-managed synonym list, exact alias matching first and stable ordering. No language model, no embeddings. Only published, in-review-window entries for the caller's audience are searchable. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 4.

**Review cadence (proposed, `AP-GOV-06`):** commercial entries every 3 months; service entries every 6 months; any entry immediately when its source file changes. A CI check that flags entries whose source key changed is a Phase 3 candidate.
