## Your new website, explained

### What a project includes

Agreed messaging, page structure, a responsive build that works well on phones, search foundations (metadata, canonical URLs, structured data, headings, internal links, indexation controls and page speed) and a clear route from visitor to enquiry, with launch support for that scope. Your proposal is the definitive list.

### What is separate unless your proposal includes it

Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support. Managed business email is also separate unless combined in writing.

### Price

Website design and development starts from £2,000. That is a starting point for an agreed scope, not unlimited design, content, integrations, marketing or support. Your quote is based on your requirements, the complexity of the journeys and systems, and the deliverables we write down.

### Timing

We confirm timing after discovery. Content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk affect the schedule more than the number of pages. The proposal records the delivery range and its assumptions.

### What we need from you

Information about what you sell and who buys it; what your current site does well; any evidence you have (analytics, Search Console, enquiry records); content, images and brand assets; and access to your domain, hosting and any connected systems. Projects move fastest when these are identified early.

### Ownership

Ownership of the bespoke work is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once the agreed fees are paid. You keep your own materials, trademarks and business data.

### Editing your site

If you expect to change content often, we can build an editable content layer. Tell us what you expect to change and how often, and the proposal will say exactly what is editable.

### Moving from your current site

We review what the current site already does well (pages that rank, enquiries, integrations and hosting) before recommending a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration. When we migrate, we map existing URLs to their new equivalents with redirects, carry over content that performs, preserve metadata and check indexing after launch. Any rebuild carries some search risk, and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings.

### Hosting

Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service. We choose it around the workload and support model, and document who is accountable.

## Being found: search and AI search

### What SEO is

Search engine optimisation is the work that makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results: technical foundations, content that answers real searches, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work.

### Local SEO

For people searching for a provider in a place: clear service and area pages, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.

### Technical SEO

Crawlability, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. Content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.

### AI search and answer engine optimisation (AEO)

*[DRAFT: new wording, founder approval required]* More people now ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Those systems work best with clear, accurate, well-structured information. We build pages that answer buyers' real questions directly, keep facts consistent, and use structured data and FAQ content. Nobody can control or guarantee what an AI system says about a business, because those systems are run by third parties and change often.

### What to expect

Technical fixes can change indexation quickly; content and authority work is measured over months. No one can guarantee first place on Google. We commit to the work, and to measuring it against a recorded baseline.

### In a new build, and afterwards

########## R10-technical-escalation-guide.md
# R10 Technical escalation guide

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT` |
| Audience | Partner only |
| Review owner | Delivery founder |
| Sources | Meeting types in `admin/src/lib/expansion-operations.ts`; faq: something-breaks, manage-external-site, unfinished-project, website-migration, dns, domains |
| Review questions | Confirm routes. Confirm "urgent" examples and how founders want to be told about them. |

## Which request to raise

| Situation | Meeting type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Migration, platform change, domain or hosting move | `technical_scoping` | Always before price or timeline |
| E-commerce, booking, payments, portals, integrations | `technical_scoping` | |
| A workflow, CRM or system rather than a website | `bespoke_discovery` | See R05 |
| Prospect ready for detail | `joint_sales` | Brief ScaleSmiths first |
| Pricing, payment plans, discounts, contract questions | `commercial_assistance` | Never answer these yourself |
| Reviewing a proposal before it is sent | `proposal_review` | |
| Wanting help with a topic | `training` | Optional |
| Complaint, mistake, legal question, data concern, urgent client problem | `escalation` | Same day |

## Always escalate

- The client's live website, email or domain is broken now. Under an agreed arrangement, ScaleSmiths follows the documented route; without one, ScaleSmiths will say honestly whether it can help.
- Someone offers you passwords. Decline; ScaleSmiths uses delegated or scoped access.
- The client wants ScaleSmiths to take over an unfinished project or a site it did not build (a code and infrastructure review comes first).
- Security incidents, suspected hacking, data loss or anything involving personal data.
- A question you cannot answer from an approved knowledge entry.

## What to include

1. Business name and portal reference.
2. What the client asked, in their words.
3. What you have already said.
4. Relevant facts from the questionnaire (systems, access, deadline).
5. How urgent it is, and why.

## What happens next

ScaleSmiths reviews the request and confirms a time, proposes an alternative or asks for information. Nothing is booked, and no invitation is sent, until a time is confirmed.

# R11 Commercial pricing reference

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`. The figures are `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED`; this reference document is not approved |
| Audience | Partner only |
| Review owner | Founders, accountant |
| Sources | `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts`, `web/src/lib/engagement-models.ts`, faq: cost, project-pricing, deposit, outside-nottingham |
| Review questions | Confirm figures at each review. Should partners refer to the budget options on the public project brief? |

> Implementation note: when built, this page must render prices from `published-starting-prices.ts`, not from copied text, so that it cannot drift from the public site.

## Published client prices (GBP, VAT treatment per proposal)

| Offer | Published price | Published note |
|---|---|---|
| Website design and development | From £2,000 | Content, pages, integrations, migration and support are set in the proposal |
| Growth Partnership | From £350 per month | An entry point for an agreed scope; not an unlimited marketing package |
| Business Growth Audit | £395 | One-time review and prioritised roadmap; where the published terms apply, the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build |
| Business email | From £15 per month | Three 5GB mailboxes on your domain, initial setup included; extra mailboxes not included unless agreed |
| Established transformation, custom platforms, enterprise | Scoped after discovery | Never sold against a website starting price |

**Starting-price boundary (quote it as written):** "A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed result. Every proposal depends on requirements, complexity and the deliverables we write down. Prices are in GBP. We do not bill in other currencies or publish fixed converted prices."

## Rules

- Quote only the figures above, always with the boundary.
- Do not estimate final prices, ranges for custom work, or monthly costs for hosting.
- Payment terms are set per proposal. There is no blanket deposit policy to describe.
- GBP only. Do not convert to other currencies.
- Discounts: none are available to partners. *[PROPOSED POLICY: founder-reserved discount allowances exist in the software but none is approved.]*

*[FOUNDER DECISION: VAT wording for partners to use when a client asks whether prices include VAT.]*
########## R12-commission-and-payment-reference.md
# R12 Commission and payment reference

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED`. Every term below is `PROPOSED POLICY` |
| Audience | Partner only. Never share with clients |
| Review owner | Founders, accountant, solicitor |
| Sources | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../../COMMISSION-RULES.md), [COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md](../../intelligence/COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md), [DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md](../../intelligence/DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md), [PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md](../../intelligence/PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md), [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) |
| Blocking decisions | Final partner agreement; twelve-month terms and eligible payment definitions; withdrawal policy; refund and clawback treatment; partner invoices and VAT; achievement and referral terms; market approval |

> **This is not an offer, agreement or promise of payment.** It illustrates the proposed programme. The partner agreement, once approved, is the only source of entitlement. All plans are disabled in the software until founders enable them.

## How commission is proposed to work

- Rate: 30% (3,000 basis points) of **eligible payments actually collected**, excluding VAT.
- Standard website plan: commission on the build fee and on the **first** Growth Partnership payment. Later monthly payments earn no acquisition commission.
- Growth Partnership only: commission on the first monthly payment.
- Bespoke: 30% of eligible collected value, unless a different rate is approved in writing for that quote.
- Only payments a founder has verified as collected count. Each has an external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference.
- Calculated once on the cumulative total, so splitting a payment cannot change the result.
- A pending contract value is never earned.

## Illustrations (accountant review required)

| Scenario | Eligible collected (ex VAT) | Proposed commission |
|---|---|---|
| Standard: £2,000 build + first £350 | £2,350 | £705 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,500 + £350 | £1,850 | £555 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,000 + £350 | £1,350 | £405 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £500 + £350 | £850 | £255 |
| Free build (founder-approved) + £350 | £350 | £105 |
| Bespoke, £10,000 collected | £10,000 | £3,000 |
| Bespoke, £50,000 collected | £50,000 | £15,000 |

Payment schedule examples from the draft programme: equal instalments (£1,000 deposit, £1,000 final balance, £350 first Growth Partnership payment), or deposit and completion (£750 and £1,250, then £350). Either way the standard total is £705.

The draft programme also models a twelve-month minimum term and a minimum contract value of £6,200 (£2,000 + 12 × £350). This is a client contract term under review, not a partner entitlement.

## Refunds

Under the current software default, a refund on a commissionable payment is **held for founder review**; nothing is deducted automatically. Whether earned commission is adjusted after a refund is an open legal and accounting decision.

## Withdrawals and payment

Withdrawal requests are built but **not operational**: no frequency, minimum, invoicing or VAT policy is approved. *[FOUNDER DECISION]*

## Planned rewards (not payable)

Achievement rewards and the £250 partner referral reward are **planned and conditional**. The software refuses to approve any reward until a programme version is approved in writing. Do not mention them to anyone as earnings.

## Markets

No market is approved yet, including the UK. A contract cannot be accepted for a customer in an unapproved market. GBP only.
########## R13-follow-up-templates.md
# R13 Professional follow-up templates

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`; each template needs approval |
| Audience | Client-facing (sent by the partner to a prospect who has agreed to be contacted) |
| Review owner | Both founders; privacy adviser (`AP-PRIV-01`, `AP-LEG-03`) |
| Review questions | Approved sign-off and title (`AP-GOV-05`)? Must templates include an opt-out line? Approved channels? |

Rules: send only to people you have spoken to who agreed to hear from you; personalise every message; no pressure or false urgency; include only published prices; stop if asked.

## T1 After a discovery conversation

> Subject: Our conversation about [business name]
>
> Hello [name],
>
> Thank you for your time today. To summarise what you told me:
>
> - [point 1]
> - [point 2]
>
> The next step we agreed was [next step]. [If a quote: I'll ask ScaleSmiths to prepare a proper quote, and they will be in touch directly.]
>
> I'll check back on [date] unless you'd prefer otherwise.
>
> Kind regards,
> [name]
> Independent partner of ScaleSmiths *[title pending `AP-GOV-05`]*

## T2 Suggesting the Business Growth Audit

> Hello [name],
>
> Following our chat, a good first step might be the ScaleSmiths Business Growth Audit. It's a one-time review (£395) that produces a prioritised roadmap for the website and search presence. Where the published terms apply, the full fee is credited against an eligible ScaleSmiths build afterwards.
>
> You can read about it here: [audit page link]. Happy to answer any questions.
>
> Kind regards, [name]

## T3 Introducing ScaleSmiths for a joint meeting

> Hello [name],
>
> As discussed, I'd like to introduce you to ScaleSmiths so they can go through [topic] in more detail. Could you let me know two or three times that suit you over the next couple of weeks?
>
> Kind regards, [name]

## T4 After "we need to think about it"

> Hello [name],
>
> Thanks again for considering it. I've attached a short guide [approved resource] in case it helps. I'll check in on [date]; if the timing isn't right, just let me know and I won't chase.
>
> Kind regards, [name]

## T5 Closing the loop respectfully

> Hello [name],
>
> I haven't heard back, so I'll assume now isn't the right time. I won't contact you again about this, but you're very welcome to get in touch whenever it would be useful.
>
> Kind regards, [name]

## T6 Acknowledging a request not to be contacted

> Hello [name],
>
> Understood. I've noted that you'd prefer not to be contacted, and I've passed this on to ScaleSmiths. Apologies for any inconvenience.
>
> Kind regards, [name]

# Empower implementation phases (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** No phase may start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155)) is merged with branch protection applied (`AP-B0`). Each phase ships behind its own flag, defaulting off, and needs a separate deployment approval under the existing release runbook. Acceptance criteria are in [ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md](ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md).

## Phase 0: B1 planning (this package)

- Deliverable: this folder. No code.
- Exit gate: founders review the package and record initial decisions in [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md), at least `AP-GOV-04`, `AP-GOV-06`, `AP-DES-01` and `AP-ENG-01` to `AP-ENG-04`.

## Phase 1: content foundation and founder workspace

**Scope**
- Migration: `empower_content_items`, `empower_content_versions`, `empower_content_approvals`, `empower_content_links`, lifecycle trigger, one-published-version partial unique index, audit events.
- Content service: create item, create version, submit, request changes, approve, publish, supersede, archive; field validation per kind; audience lint; link allow-list.
- Restricted Markdown renderer (server-side, HTML disabled, sanitised).
- Founder Content workspace in `/expansion` (W7), including diff view, pre-flight checks and preview as partner.
- Seed script that loads this package's drafts as `draft` versions only.
- Flag: `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED`.

**Not in scope:** any partner-facing route.

**Entry gate:** `AP-B0`; decisions `AP-GOV-04`, `AP-GOV-06`, `AP-ENG-01`, `AP-ENG-02`.
**Exit gate:** acceptance criteria P1 pass in CI; migration reviewed by the `db-migration-reviewer` agent and a founder; deployment approved.

## Phase 2: Resource Centre and knowledge search for partners

**Scope**
- Partner routes `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge` (W4, W5), and the objection workspace (W6).
- PostgreSQL full-text search with synonyms and exact alias match; zero-result logging.
- Read adapter for legacy `expansion_resources`.
- "Request help" from an entry opens the existing meeting request with type and reference.
- Toolkit linking for `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents`.
- Flag: `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED`.

**Content gate:** at least the client-facing service resources (R03 to R06), R07 to R10, R11 and the non-commercial knowledge entries approved and published. R12, KB-COMM-* and C11 stay unpublished until the financial decisions are made.

**Entry gate:** Phase 1 accepted; `AP-PRIV-01`, `AP-PRIV-02`; partner activation itself is still governed by the B0 gates (`PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED`).
**Exit gate:** acceptance criteria P2 pass; browser checks on mobile and desktop; deployment approved.

## Phase 3: Partner Academy

**Scope**
- Tables `empower_courses`, `empower_modules`, `empower_lessons`, `empower_progress`.
- Partner routes `/partner/academy` and children (W1 to W3), private progress, optional self-checks.
- Founder course structure editor and aggregate progress view.
- Toolkit `academy` item can then be set to available by a founder, with evidence.
- Flag: `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED`.

**Content gate:** C01, C02, C08, C09, C10 and C12 approved as a minimum launch set (C12 needs the agreement). C07 and C11 follow when unblocked.

**Entry gate:** Phase 2 accepted; `AP-GOV-02` (solicitor), `AP-GOV-03`, `AP-GOV-05`.
**Exit gate:** acceptance criteria P3 pass; deployment approved; the `/partners` availability label for "Partner Academy" is updated only through a separate founder-approved content change.

## Phase 4: refinements (candidates, not commitments)

- Source-drift check: CI flags knowledge entries whose cited `faq-library.ts` key or `published-starting-prices.ts` value changed.
- Commercial figures rendered from `partner-programme.ts` constants with plan version stamps.
- PDF export of client-facing resources.
- `pg_trgm` typo tolerance.
- Self-hosted Syne in the admin app (`AP-DES-02`) and token clean-up (`AP-ENG-05`).
- Client portal delivery of client-facing resources (separate decision).

## Dependencies at a glance

```
B0 merged ─► P1 founder workspace ─► content approved ─► P2 Resource Centre ─► P3 Academy ─► P4
                                         ▲                       ▲                ▲
                       AP-GOV-04/06, ENG-01/02        AP-PRIV-01/02      AP-GOV-02/03/05, agreement
```
# Empower acceptance criteria (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Each criterion should be verified by an automated test unless marked *(manual)*. Phases are defined in [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md).

## Phase 0: planning package

- [x] Package exists under `docs/expansion/empower/` with architecture, curriculum, lesson content, resource drafts, knowledge inventory, wireframes, approval register, phases, acceptance criteria and security model.
- [x] Every item carries an approval status; no item is marked approved.
- [x] `node scripts/check-documentation-links.mjs` passes.
- [ ] Founders have reviewed the package *(manual)*.

## Phase 1: content foundation

**Lifecycle and integrity**
1. A version's title, body, fields, sources, author and creation time cannot be updated; attempts fail at the database.
2. Versions cannot be deleted.
3. Only the transitions in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 3.1 succeed; all others fail at both service and database.
4. `in_review → approved` fails without an approval row by a founder; fails when the approver is the author while two founders are active; succeeds with a recorded override reason when only one founder is active.
5. Publishing a version supersedes the previous published version in the same transaction; at most one published version per item exists, including under concurrent publishes (real-PostgreSQL test on separate connections).
6. An item's audience cannot be changed after creation.
7. Every transition writes an audit row with actor, item, version and event.

**Validation**
8. A knowledge version without question, answer, client explanation, source, limitation or escalation cannot be submitted.
9. A client-facing version containing blocked terms cannot be submitted without an override reason, which is audited.
10. Links outside internal routes and the allow-list are rejected.
11. Rendered output contains no raw HTML from the body; script and event-handler payloads are neutralised (renderer tests with known XSS vectors).

**Access**
12. A partner account receives 403 for every founder content action and the founder Content workspace.
13. An owner or administrator cannot reach any `/partner` route (existing RBAC rule still holds).
14. With `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` off, the Content workspace is not reachable.

**Seeding**
15. The seed script creates only `draft` versions and is idempotent.

## Phase 2: Resource Centre and knowledge search

**Serving**
1. Partners receive only versions that are `published`, within `review_by`, and permitted for their audience; drafts, approved-but-unpublished, superseded, archived and expired versions are never returned (service and browser tests).
2. Audience filtering happens in SQL; no request parameter can widen it.
3. Every rendered item shows audience ribbon, version, approval date and review-by date.
4. Copy controls appear only on client-facing content.
5. With `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` off, partner routes return 404 and navigation hides them.

**Search**
6. Identical queries over identical content return identical ordering.
7. Exact alias matches rank above full-text matches.
8. Synonyms expand queries as configured (for example "ssl" finds the HTTPS entry).
9. A search never returns unpublished, expired or other-audience content, and a zero-result response is identical whether matching content is hidden or absent.
10. Query input over 200 characters is rejected; search is rate-limited per partner.
11. Zero-result queries are logged with a hashed partner id and purged after the approved retention period.
12. p95 search latency under 200ms with 1,000 published entries on CI hardware.

**Integration**
13. "Request help" opens a meeting request pre-filled with the entry's escalation type and reference; nothing is booked automatically.
14. Legacy published `expansion_resources` appear in the library through the read adapter, labelled as legacy.

**Experience** *(manual plus automated accessibility checks)*
15. Knowledge search, resource library and objection workspace are usable at 320px width without horizontal scrolling.
16. Automated accessibility checks report no serious or critical violations; colour-contrast tokens meet the values in [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md).
17. All functions are keyboard operable; `/` focuses search.

## Phase 3: Partner Academy

1. Courses, modules and lessons appear only when their content versions are published and within review.
2. Progress is visible only to the partner who created it; founders see aggregate counts only, unless the partner has opted in (if `AP-GOV-03` allows it).
3. No query from commission, allocation, recognition, achievements, referrals or withdrawals reads progress tables (static test over the server modules).
4. Knowledge-check answers are not persisted; only `check_attempted` is stored.
5. No course is marked required, and no UI text uses "must complete", "deadline" or "score" (copy test).
6. When a lesson is superseded, partners who read the old version see "Updated since you read it".
7. With `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` off, Academy routes return 404.
8. Lesson pages meet the same width, keyboard and contrast criteria as Phase 2.

## Content release criteria (every content version)

- Status is approved by a founder with a reference and review-by date.
- Every factual statement traces to a source in its `source_refs`.
- No guaranteed outcome, invented proof, unpublished price or unapproved commercial term.
- Partner-only material contains nothing marked client-facing, and the reverse.
- Proposed policy is labelled as proposed.

# Empower acceptance criteria (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Each criterion should be verified by an automated test unless marked *(manual)*. Phases are defined in [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md).

## Phase 0: planning package

- [x] Package exists under `docs/expansion/empower/` with architecture, curriculum, lesson content, resource drafts, knowledge inventory, wireframes, approval register, phases, acceptance criteria and security model.
- [x] Every item carries an approval status; no item is marked approved.
- [x] `node scripts/check-documentation-links.mjs` passes.
- [ ] Founders have reviewed the package *(manual)*.

## Phase 1: content foundation

**Lifecycle and integrity**
1. A version's title, body, fields, sources, author and creation time cannot be updated; attempts fail at the database.
2. Versions cannot be deleted.
3. Only the transitions in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 3.1 succeed; all others fail at both service and database.
4. `in_review → approved` fails without an approval row by a founder; fails when the approver is the author while two founders are active; succeeds with a recorded override reason when only one founder is active.
5. Publishing a version supersedes the previous published version in the same transaction; at most one published version per item exists, including under concurrent publishes (real-PostgreSQL test on separate connections).
6. An item's audience cannot be changed after creation.
7. Every transition writes an audit row with actor, item, version and event.

**Validation**
8. A knowledge version without question, answer, client explanation, source, limitation or escalation cannot be submitted.
9. A client-facing version containing blocked terms cannot be submitted without an override reason, which is audited.
10. Links outside internal routes and the allow-list are rejected.
11. Rendered output contains no raw HTML from the body; script and event-handler payloads are neutralised (renderer tests with known XSS vectors).

**Access**
12. A partner account receives 403 for every founder content action and the founder Content workspace.
13. An owner or administrator cannot reach any `/partner` route (existing RBAC rule still holds).
14. With `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` off, the Content workspace is not reachable.

**Seeding**
15. The seed script creates only `draft` versions and is idempotent.

## Phase 2: Resource Centre and knowledge search

**Serving**
1. Partners receive only versions that are `published`, within `review_by`, and permitted for their audience; drafts, approved-but-unpublished, superseded, archived and expired versions are never returned (service and browser tests).
2. Audience filtering happens in SQL; no request parameter can widen it.
3. Every rendered item shows audience ribbon, version, approval date and review-by date.
4. Copy controls appear only on client-facing content.
5. With `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` off, partner routes return 404 and navigation hides them.

**Search**
6. Identical queries over identical content return identical ordering.
7. Exact alias matches rank above full-text matches.
8. Synonyms expand queries as configured (for example "ssl" finds the HTTPS entry).
9. A search never returns unpublished, expired or other-audience content, and a zero-result response is identical whether matching content is hidden or absent.
10. Query input over 200 characters is rejected; search is rate-limited per partner.
11. Zero-result queries are logged with a hashed partner id and purged after the approved retention period.
12. p95 search latency under 200ms with 1,000 published entries on CI hardware.

**Integration**
13. "Request help" opens a meeting request pre-filled with the entry's escalation type and reference; nothing is booked automatically.
14. Legacy published `expansion_resources` appear in the library through the read adapter, labelled as legacy.

**Experience** *(manual plus automated accessibility checks)*
15. Knowledge search, resource library and objection workspace are usable at 320px width without horizontal scrolling.
16. Automated accessibility checks report no serious or critical violations; colour-contrast tokens meet the values in [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md).
17. All functions are keyboard operable; `/` focuses search.

## Phase 3: Partner Academy

1. Courses, modules and lessons appear only when their content versions are published and within review.
2. Progress is visible only to the partner who created it; founders see aggregate counts only, unless the partner has opted in (if `AP-GOV-03` allows it).
3. No query from commission, allocation, recognition, achievements, referrals or withdrawals reads progress tables (static test over the server modules).
4. Knowledge-check answers are not persisted; only `check_attempted` is stored.
5. No course is marked required, and no UI text uses "must complete", "deadline" or "score" (copy test).
6. When a lesson is superseded, partners who read the old version see "Updated since you read it".
7. With `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` off, Academy routes return 404.
8. Lesson pages meet the same width, keyboard and contrast criteria as Phase 2.

## Content release criteria (every content version)

- Status is approved by a founder with a reference and review-by date.
- Every factual statement traces to a source in its `source_refs`.
- No guaranteed outcome, invented proof, unpublished price or unapproved commercial term.
- Partner-only material contains nothing marked client-facing, and the reverse.
- Proposed policy is labelled as proposed.

# Empower design specification

**Status: DRAFT.** Visual direction for the Academy, Resource Centre and founder publishing interface. Screen-level layouts are in [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md). Brand changes need founder approval (`AP-DES-01`).

## 1. Direction

**Quiet premium.** Black and charcoal surfaces, metallic gold used sparingly as a signal of quality and of "approved", silver for secondary emphasis, generous spacing, clear typography, minimal navigation. The interface should feel calm and trustworthy: a partner is about to speak to a client and needs the right answer fast. Search comes first; decoration never competes with content.

Principles:

1. **Content first.** Text measures 60 to 75 characters on large screens; nothing decorative inside reading areas.
2. **Gold means something.** Gold marks primary actions, the active item and approval ribbons. It is not used for body text or large fills.
3. **Status is never colour alone.** Every status has a text label and an icon.
4. **Mobile is a first-class target.** Partners will read lessons and look up answers on phones before meetings.
5. **Reuse before invent.** Build on the admin tokens and the `ex-*` portal patterns.

## 2. Reconciling the two existing systems

The Partner Portal is part of the admin app, so Empower uses the **admin token set** as its base and borrows silver from the public site. It does not import the public site's warm palette wholesale, which would make the portal inconsistent with the rest of the admin shell.

| Role | Empower token | Value | Origin | Contrast (measured) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page background | `--bg` | `#131416` | admin | — |
| Raised surface | `--s1` | `#1a1b1e` | admin | — |
| Card surface | `--s2` | `#222428` | admin | — |
| Hover surface | `--s3` | `#2a2d31` | admin | — |
| Primary text | `--t1` | `#f1f5f9` | admin | 16.82:1 on `--bg` |
| Secondary text | `--t2` | `#a6b0be` | admin | 7.85:1 on `--s1`; 7.09:1 on `--s2` |
| Muted text (new) | `--emp-muted` | `#8a93a3` | new | 5.95:1 on `--bg`; 5.02:1 on `--s2` |
| Decorative text only | `--t3` | `#667085` | admin | **3.71:1 on `--bg`: fails AA for body text**; use only for disabled states and decoration |
| Metallic gold (solid) | `--acc` | `#d1b266` | admin | 9.01:1 on `--bg`; 7.60:1 on `--s2` |
| Gold gradient (decoration) | `--emp-gold` | `linear-gradient(135deg,#e6cf8f 0%,#d1b266 45%,#a8873f 100%)` | new, from `--acc` | Dark text `#131416` on it: 5.44:1 at the darkest stop |
| Silver | `--emp-silver` | `#cfc7bc` | public `--silver` | 11.01:1 on `--bg`; 9.29:1 on `--s2` |
| Silver line | `--emp-silver-line` | `rgba(207,199,188,.18)` | new | — |
| Approved | `--grn` | `#10b981` | admin | 6.79:1 on `--s1` |
| Review due / draft | `--amb` | `#f59e0b` | admin | 8.02:1 on `--s1` |
| Blocked / withdrawn | `--red` | `#ef4444` | admin | used with a label |

Contrast values were calculated with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (the same method as `web/src/lib/color-contrast.ts`). They must be asserted in tests at implementation, as the public site already does.

**Clean-up recommended alongside:** `expansion.css` hard-codes `#131416`, `#18191b`, `#edf0f5` and `#c3a86c`. Empower styles should use tokens only; replacing the hard-coded portal values is a small, separate change (`AP-ENG-05`).

## 3. Typography

| Use | Family | Size / line height | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display (course titles, page titles) | `--font-syne` (admin resolves this to Arial Black) | 28/34 desktop, 24/30 mobile | 700 |
| Section heading | Inter | 20/28 | 600 |
| Body and lesson text | Inter | 17/28 (lesson), 15/24 (UI) | 400 |
| Labels, overlines | Inter, uppercase, letter-spacing .14em | 11/16 | 600 |
| Data and figures | Inter, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (as `.ex-money`) | as context | 500 |

Decision `AP-DES-02`: whether to self-host Syne in the admin app (as the public site does) so display type matches the brand. Until decided, the existing fallback stays.

## 4. Layout and spacing

- 8px spacing grid; page gutter 16px mobile, 24px tablet, 36px desktop (matching `.ex-header`).
- Max content width 1200px; reading column 720px.
- Radius: 8px cards (admin `--radius-md`), 12px feature panels (as `.ex-research`), 999px chips.
- Elevation: borders before shadows; `--shadow-raised` only for overlays.
- Breakpoints: 640px, 960px, 1280px.

## 5. Components

| Component | Specification | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| Portal shell | Existing header and tab navigation. Empower adds three entries: Academy, Resources, Knowledge | `ExpansionWorkspace` items |
| Search bar | Full width, 52px tall, silver 1px border, gold focus ring (3px, `rgba(209,178,102,.28)`), keyboard shortcut `/` | `.field-control` pattern |
| Course card | `--s2` surface, 2px gold-gradient top edge, overline (course number), title, one-line purpose, lesson count and reading time, progress ring (private), status chip | `.ex-panel` |
| Status chip | Pill with icon and text: Approved · v3 · review by 12 Mar 2027; Partner only; Client-facing; Updated since you read it | `.ex-badge` |
| Audience ribbon | Full-width strip above content: silver "Partner only: do not share" or gold-outlined "Client-facing: approved for sharing" | new |
| Lesson body | Reading column, 17px text, callouts for "Say it like this" (gold left rule), "Avoid" (red left rule, labelled), "Escalate when" (silver left rule) | new |
| Knowledge result | Question (heading), client explanation (first), limitation, escalation, source, status chip | new |
| Copy control | Only on client-facing text; announces "Copied" via `aria-live` | new |
| Empty state | One sentence and a next action, as in the existing `Empty` component | `Empty` |
| Founder diff view | Side-by-side or inline diff between versions, additions in green, removals struck through, with labels | new |

## 6. Motion

Subtle and optional: 150 to 200ms fades for panels and chips, no parallax, no animated gradients. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (the admin already does for its workspace).

## 7. Accessibility requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA as the target for these screens (an engineering target, not a public claim).
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, logical heading order, skip link to search.
- Status conveyed by text and icon as well as colour.
- Lesson text resizable to 200% without horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- Knowledge checks: answers announced via `aria-live`; no time limits.
# Empower wireframe descriptions

**Status: DRAFT.** Low-fidelity descriptions for design and engineering. Tokens and components are in [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md). All partner screens sit inside the existing portal shell at `/partner`, behind the `expansion.partner` capability and the feature flags in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). Labels such as "Approved · v2" in the sketches are illustrative placeholders showing where approval metadata appears; they do not mean any item is approved.

## W1 Academy dashboard (`/partner/academy`)

```
┌ Portal header ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Overview  Prospects  Resources  Knowledge  [Academy]  Commission  …   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ PARTNER ACADEMY                                                        │
│ Learn at your own pace. Optional and voluntary.                        │
│ [ Search lessons…                                              / ]     │
│                                                                        │
│ Continue where you left off   ┌──────────────┐                         │
│                               │ C04 · L3     │  (only if any progress)  │
│                               └──────────────┘                         │
│ Courses                                                                │
│ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐                              │
│ │▔▔ gold ▔▔ │ │           │ │           │   3 columns ≥960px,          │
│ │ C01       │ │ C02       │ │ C03       │   2 at ≥640px, 1 on mobile   │
│ │ Welcome…  │ │ Website…  │ │ SEO…      │                              │
│ │ 7 lessons │ │ 8 lessons │ │ 8 lessons │                              │
│ │ ◔ 2 of 7  │ │ Not opened│ │ Updated   │                              │
│ └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘                              │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- Header copy states the Academy is optional. No completion percentages across the whole Academy, no leaderboard, no "required" badges.
- Progress ring and "continue" card are private and can be hidden by the partner.
- Courses not yet published do not appear (no "coming soon" teasers that imply a promise).

# Empower design specification

**Status: DRAFT.** Visual direction for the Academy, Resource Centre and founder publishing interface. Screen-level layouts are in [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md). Brand changes need founder approval (`AP-DES-01`).

## 1. Direction

**Quiet premium.** Black and charcoal surfaces, metallic gold used sparingly as a signal of quality and of "approved", silver for secondary emphasis, generous spacing, clear typography, minimal navigation. The interface should feel calm and trustworthy: a partner is about to speak to a client and needs the right answer fast. Search comes first; decoration never competes with content.

Principles:

1. **Content first.** Text measures 60 to 75 characters on large screens; nothing decorative inside reading areas.
2. **Gold means something.** Gold marks primary actions, the active item and approval ribbons. It is not used for body text or large fills.
3. **Status is never colour alone.** Every status has a text label and an icon.
4. **Mobile is a first-class target.** Partners will read lessons and look up answers on phones before meetings.
5. **Reuse before invent.** Build on the admin tokens and the `ex-*` portal patterns.

## 2. Reconciling the two existing systems

The Partner Portal is part of the admin app, so Empower uses the **admin token set** as its base and borrows silver from the public site. It does not import the public site's warm palette wholesale, which would make the portal inconsistent with the rest of the admin shell.

| Role | Empower token | Value | Origin | Contrast (measured) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page background | `--bg` | `#131416` | admin | — |
| Raised surface | `--s1` | `#1a1b1e` | admin | — |
| Card surface | `--s2` | `#222428` | admin | — |
| Hover surface | `--s3` | `#2a2d31` | admin | — |
| Primary text | `--t1` | `#f1f5f9` | admin | 16.82:1 on `--bg` |
| Secondary text | `--t2` | `#a6b0be` | admin | 7.85:1 on `--s1`; 7.09:1 on `--s2` |
| Muted text (new) | `--emp-muted` | `#8a93a3` | new | 5.95:1 on `--bg`; 5.02:1 on `--s2` |
| Decorative text only | `--t3` | `#667085` | admin | **3.71:1 on `--bg`: fails AA for body text**; use only for disabled states and decoration |
| Metallic gold (solid) | `--acc` | `#d1b266` | admin | 9.01:1 on `--bg`; 7.60:1 on `--s2` |
| Gold gradient (decoration) | `--emp-gold` | `linear-gradient(135deg,#e6cf8f 0%,#d1b266 45%,#a8873f 100%)` | new, from `--acc` | Dark text `#131416` on it: 5.44:1 at the darkest stop |
| Silver | `--emp-silver` | `#cfc7bc` | public `--silver` | 11.01:1 on `--bg`; 9.29:1 on `--s2` |
| Silver line | `--emp-silver-line` | `rgba(207,199,188,.18)` | new | — |
| Approved | `--grn` | `#10b981` | admin | 6.79:1 on `--s1` |
| Review due / draft | `--amb` | `#f59e0b` | admin | 8.02:1 on `--s1` |
| Blocked / withdrawn | `--red` | `#ef4444` | admin | used with a label |

Contrast values were calculated with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (the same method as `web/src/lib/color-contrast.ts`). They must be asserted in tests at implementation, as the public site already does.

**Clean-up recommended alongside:** `expansion.css` hard-codes `#131416`, `#18191b`, `#edf0f5` and `#c3a86c`. Empower styles should use tokens only; replacing the hard-coded portal values is a small, separate change (`AP-ENG-05`).

## 3. Typography

| Use | Family | Size / line height | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display (course titles, page titles) | `--font-syne` (admin resolves this to Arial Black) | 28/34 desktop, 24/30 mobile | 700 |
| Section heading | Inter | 20/28 | 600 |
| Body and lesson text | Inter | 17/28 (lesson), 15/24 (UI) | 400 |
| Labels, overlines | Inter, uppercase, letter-spacing .14em | 11/16 | 600 |
| Data and figures | Inter, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (as `.ex-money`) | as context | 500 |

Decision `AP-DES-02`: whether to self-host Syne in the admin app (as the public site does) so display type matches the brand. Until decided, the existing fallback stays.

## 4. Layout and spacing

- 8px spacing grid; page gutter 16px mobile, 24px tablet, 36px desktop (matching `.ex-header`).
- Max content width 1200px; reading column 720px.
- Radius: 8px cards (admin `--radius-md`), 12px feature panels (as `.ex-research`), 999px chips.
- Elevation: borders before shadows; `--shadow-raised` only for overlays.
- Breakpoints: 640px, 960px, 1280px.

## 5. Components

| Component | Specification | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| Portal shell | Existing header and tab navigation. Empower adds three entries: Academy, Resources, Knowledge | `ExpansionWorkspace` items |
| Search bar | Full width, 52px tall, silver 1px border, gold focus ring (3px, `rgba(209,178,102,.28)`), keyboard shortcut `/` | `.field-control` pattern |
| Course card | `--s2` surface, 2px gold-gradient top edge, overline (course number), title, one-line purpose, lesson count and reading time, progress ring (private), status chip | `.ex-panel` |
| Status chip | Pill with icon and text: Approved · v3 · review by 12 Mar 2027; Partner only; Client-facing; Updated since you read it | `.ex-badge` |
| Audience ribbon | Full-width strip above content: silver "Partner only: do not share" or gold-outlined "Client-facing: approved for sharing" | new |
| Lesson body | Reading column, 17px text, callouts for "Say it like this" (gold left rule), "Avoid" (red left rule, labelled), "Escalate when" (silver left rule) | new |
| Knowledge result | Question (heading), client explanation (first), limitation, escalation, source, status chip | new |
| Copy control | Only on client-facing text; announces "Copied" via `aria-live` | new |
| Empty state | One sentence and a next action, as in the existing `Empty` component | `Empty` |
| Founder diff view | Side-by-side or inline diff between versions, additions in green, removals struck through, with labels | new |

## 6. Motion

Subtle and optional: 150 to 200ms fades for panels and chips, no parallax, no animated gradients. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (the admin already does for its workspace).

## 7. Accessibility requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA as the target for these screens (an engineering target, not a public claim).
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, logical heading order, skip link to search.
- Status conveyed by text and icon as well as colour.
- Lesson text resizable to 200% without horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- Knowledge checks: answers announced via `aria-live`; no time limits.

**Status: DRAFT.** Low-fidelity descriptions for design and engineering. Tokens and components are in [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md). content.content:
[outside-nottingham] Yes. ScaleSmiths is based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire and works with businesses across the UK. Published work also includes CSDS, a computer repair firm in Pennsylvania. Projects outside the area, including work with businesses overseas, run remotely with a review cadence agreed in the scope. We do not claim overseas offices or regional expertise we cannot substantiate. Proposals are quoted in GBP.

[established-businesses] Yes, and that is where most of the client work sits. Confirm-A-Kill is an established Nottinghamshire pest-control business whose website and operating systems were rebuilt around search, conversion and day-to-day delivery. Established businesses usually have real evidence === rankings, enquiries, existing systems === and the work starts by protecting what already performs.

[hosting-provided] Yes. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx setups on a VPS as well as managed platforms such as Vercel, chosen around the workload and the support model rather than sold as an anonymous storage allowance. Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service on its own.

[business-email] Yes. ScaleSmiths Managed Business Email starts at £15 per month for three custom-domain mailboxes with 5GB of storage each, and initial mailbox and DNS setup is included at no additional setup charge. It covers webmail, desktop and mobile client compatibility, aliases and forwarding, spam filtering, TLS-secured transport, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration. It is available standalone, you do not need a ScaleSmiths website.

[deposit] Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set out in the proposal and signed order for each project rather than published as a blanket policy. Ownership of bespoke deliverables transfers once the applicable agreed fees are paid. Ask during discovery and you will have the terms in writing before anything is committed.

[ecommerce-builds] Yes. Pinkys Prints is a custom e-commerce platform with catalogue variants and a tailored product admin, migrated from Shopify. We recommend custom commerce only when the operational value justifies owning it; where an established platform already fits, configuring and integrating it is usually the better decision.

[integrations] Usually, yes. Published work includes a Salon Tracker booking integration and Google and Facebook review aggregation for Glow Tanning, and Stripe subscription billing with LiveKit video for The Business Circle. We check the existing system's API, data and ownership before committing to an approach, because not every tool exposes what an integration needs.

[crm] Yes, where an off-the-shelf CRM does not fit the workflow. Confirm-A-Kill runs on a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM covering enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits and commercial service records; CSDS has a quote management admin panel behind its website. If an existing CRM already does the job, connecting the website to it is often the better investment.

[stripe] Yes. The Business Circle runs Stripe subscription billing for tiered memberships, and Prymal uses Stripe for plans, team seats and execution credits. Card details stay with the payment provider === we do not create a reason to handle them directly === and order or subscription state relies on verified server-side provider events rather than a browser redirect alone.

[customer-portals] Yes. ScaleSmiths runs its own client portal for projects, invoices, documents, messages and requests, with tenant isolation enforced server-side. The Business Circle is a published membership platform with tiered access, and VeteranFinder includes member and admin applications. Permissions and tenant boundaries are enforced on the server rather than treated as interface options.

[internal-admin-systems] Yes. Admin surfaces are a recurring part of published work: quote management for CSDS, product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints, content administration for Glow Tanning, member management for The Business Circle, and a dedicated admin console for VeteranFinder. Roles, permissions and sensitive operations are enforced server-side.

[website-ownership] Ownership of the bespoke deliverable, along with content, accounts and any third-party services, is set out in the signed project documents, and transfer follows once the agreed fees are paid. ScaleSmiths keeps its own pre-existing tools, frameworks and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences. The client service terms state this in full.

[backups] Backups are part of a managed hosting or maintenance arrangement, and the order states which environments, data and retention are covered. We are deliberately plain about the limits: backups reduce risk but do not make loss impossible, they do not replace your own continuity responsibilities, and no restoration guarantee, recovery point or recovery time is created by our online terms. Ask, and the actual arrangement is written into the agreement.

[ssl] Yes. HTTPS is a build standard, not an upsell, and certificate provisioning and renewal are part of managed hosting and deployment. The specific arrangement depends on where the site runs: platform-managed certificates on a host such as Vercel, or certificates managed at the Nginx layer on a VPS deployment.

[dns] Yes, where you give us appropriate access. Managed Business Email onboarding includes configuring the required mail and authentication records, and website or hosting work includes the DNS changes a launch or migration needs. We use delegated or scoped access where it is supported, and we never ask for domain or registrar passwords through a public form.

[after-enquiry] The founders review what you send and reply with a sensible next step. That may be a few clarifying questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal once the scope is understood. Sending the form does not take payment and does not create a contract. The quote, audit and email journeys each say what happens next on their own confirmation pages.

[ranking-guarantees] No. Rankings depend on Google's systems, your competitors and the searcher, none of which any agency controls. We will not promise a position. What can be committed to is the work itself: technical health, content that matches real search intent, credible proof, and measurement against a recorded baseline so progress is judged on evidence.

[wordpress] The websites and platforms in our published work are custom builds using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes. If you already run WordPress, we look at what it is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified.

[website-migration] Often, after a technical review of the current code, licence terms, data, deployment process and connected services. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved from managed cloud services onto self-hosted infrastructure. We map existing URLs, metadata and internal links before a migration to reduce avoidable search disruption.

[hosting-included] Not automatically. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or arranged as a managed hosting service on its own, and the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered. Managed Business Email is likewise separate unless a combined arrangement is written into the agreement.

[ranking-guarantees] No. Rankings depend on Google's systems, your competitors and the searcher, none of which any agency controls. We will not promise a position. What can be committed to is the work itself: technical health, content that matches real search intent, credible proof, and measurement against a recorded baseline so progress is judged on evidence.

[wordpress] The websites and platforms in our published work are custom builds using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes. If you already run WordPress, we look at what it is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified.

[website-migration] Often, after a technical review of the current code, licence terms, data, deployment process and connected services. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved from managed cloud services onto self-hosted infrastructure. We map existing URLs, metadata and internal links before a migration to reduce avoidable search disruption.

[hosting-included] Not automatically. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or arranged as a managed hosting service on its own, and the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered. Managed Business Email is likewise separate unless a combined arrangement is written into the agreement.

=== commission rules
5:Only authorised manual verification of qualifying VAT-exclusive collected revenue can earn commission. Each collection has an immutable external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference. Partial payments use cumulative rounding so splitting payments cannot increase entitlement. Over-collection, duplicate references with different content, invalid states and over-refunds must fail closed. Identical event replay returns the original result without a second ledger entry.
7:Custom pricing/rates require explicit founder approval; no partner can edit accepted contract terms or create financial events. Pending contractual maximum is conditional, never earned. Refunds append approved reversals with reasons under the final reviewed agreement; no automatic recovery. Payout preparation locks eligible ledger entries, binds an invoice/reference, requires manual approval and records reconciliation. Nothing in this implementation authorises transfers or self-billing.
9:Business/legal decisions still required: partner VAT treatment, applicable refund entitlement, invoice requirements, dispute resolution, lead protection term, applicant retention and agreement language. These are release prerequisites, not automated legal conclusions.

# R12 Commission and payment reference

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED`. Every term below is `PROPOSED POLICY` |
| Audience | Partner only. Never share with clients |
| Review owner | Founders, accountant, solicitor |
| Sources | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../../COMMISSION-RULES.md), [COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md](../../intelligence/COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md), [DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md](../../intelligence/DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md), [PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md](../../intelligence/PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md), [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) |
| Blocking decisions | Final partner agreement; twelve-month terms and eligible payment definitions; withdrawal policy; refund and clawback treatment; partner invoices and VAT; achievement and referral terms; market approval |

> **This is not an offer, agreement or promise of payment.** It illustrates the proposed programme. The partner agreement, once approved, is the only source of entitlement. All plans are disabled in the software until founders enable them.

## How commission is proposed to work

- Rate: 30% (3,000 basis points) of **eligible payments actually collected**, excluding VAT.
- Standard website plan: commission on the build fee and on the **first** Growth Partnership payment. Later monthly payments earn no acquisition commission.
- Growth Partnership only: commission on the first monthly payment.
- Bespoke: 30% of eligible collected value, unless a different rate is approved in writing for that quote.
- Only payments a founder has verified as collected count. Each has an external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference.
- Calculated once on the cumulative total, so splitting a payment cannot change the result.
- A pending contract value is never earned.

## Illustrations (accountant review required)

| Scenario | Eligible collected (ex VAT) | Proposed commission |
|---|---|---|
| Standard: £2,000 build + first £350 | £2,350 | £705 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,500 + £350 | £1,850 | £555 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,000 + £350 | £1,350 | £405 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £500 + £350 | £850 | £255 |
| Free build (founder-approved) + £350 | £350 | £105 |
| Bespoke, £10,000 collected | £10,000 | £3,000 |
| Bespoke, £50,000 collected | £50,000 | £15,000 |

Payment schedule examples from the draft programme: equal instalments (£1,000 deposit, £1,000 final balance, £350 first Growth Partnership payment), or deposit and completion (£750 and £1,250, then £350). Either way the standard total is £705.

The draft programme also models a twelve-month minimum term and a minimum contract value of £6,200 (£2,000 + 12 × £350). This is a client contract term under review, not a partner entitlement.

## Refunds

Under the current software default, a refund on a commissionable payment is **held for founder review**; nothing is deducted automatically. Whether earned commission is adjusted after a refund is an open legal and accounting decision.

## Withdrawals and payment

Withdrawal requests are built but **not operational**: no frequency, minimum, invoicing or VAT policy is approved. *[FOUNDER DECISION]*

## Planned rewards (not payable)

Achievement rewards and the £250 partner referral reward are **planned and conditional**. The software refuses to approve any reward until a programme version is approved in writing. Do not mention them to anyone as earnings.

## Markets

No market is approved yet, including the UK. A contract cannot be accepted for a customer in an unapproved market. GBP only.

# R12 Commission and payment reference

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED`. Every term below is `PROPOSED POLICY` |
| Audience | Partner only. Never share with clients |
| Review owner | Founders, accountant, solicitor |
| Sources | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`, [COMMISSION-RULES.md](../../COMMISSION-RULES.md), [COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md](../../intelligence/COMMERCIAL-INTEGRATION.md), [DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md](../../intelligence/DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md), [PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md](../../intelligence/PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md), [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) |
| Blocking decisions | Final partner agreement; twelve-month terms and eligible payment definitions; withdrawal policy; refund and clawback treatment; partner invoices and VAT; achievement and referral terms; market approval |

> **This is not an offer, agreement or promise of payment.** It illustrates the proposed programme. The partner agreement, once approved, is the only source of entitlement. All plans are disabled in the software until founders enable them.

## How commission is proposed to work

- Rate: 30% (3,000 basis points) of **eligible payments actually collected**, excluding VAT.
- Standard website plan: commission on the build fee and on the **first** Growth Partnership payment. Later monthly payments earn no acquisition commission.
- Growth Partnership only: commission on the first monthly payment.
- Bespoke: 30% of eligible collected value, unless a different rate is approved in writing for that quote.
- Only payments a founder has verified as collected count. Each has an external reference, invoice link, verifier and evidence reference.
- Current plans pool build payments and round once on the cumulative total, so splitting a payment cannot increase the result. Historical `standard-v1` agreements keep per-milestone rounding (differences of a few pence).
- A pending contract value is never earned.
- Commission is acquisition commission only. There is no ongoing monthly commission on later Growth Partnership payments.

## Illustrations (accountant review required)

| Scenario | Eligible collected (ex VAT) | Proposed commission |
|---|---|---|
| Standard: £2,000 build + first £350 | £2,350 | £705 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,500 + £350 | £1,850 | £555 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £1,000 + £350 | £1,350 | £405 |
| Founder-approved discounted build £500 + £350 | £850 | £255 |
| Free build (founder-approved) + £350 | £350 | £105 |
| Bespoke, £10,000 collected | £10,000 | £3,000 |
| Bespoke, £50,000 collected | £50,000 | £15,000 |

Payment schedule examples from the draft programme: equal instalments (£1,000 deposit, £1,000 final balance, £350 first Growth Partnership payment), or deposit and completion (£750 and £1,250, then £350). Either way the standard total is £705.

The draft programme also models a twelve-month minimum term and a minimum contract value of £6,200 (£2,000 + 12 × £350). This is a client contract term under review, not a partner entitlement.

Discounted and free builds exist in the software only as founder-reserved allowances; no allowance quantity, eligibility or free-build criterion is approved, so these rows illustrate arithmetic, not an available option.

## Historical agreements

Agreements already accepted under the earlier `standard-v1` plan (six-month term, £4,100 minimum contract value) keep the terms under which they were accepted; the engine leaves them unchanged. New agreements use the plan a founder selects at acceptance. Never quote the six-month term for new work. Sources: [../../intelligence/ARCHITECTURE.md](../../intelligence/ARCHITECTURE.md), [../../intelligence/COMMERCIAL-ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md](../../intelligence/COMMERCIAL-ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md).

## Refunds

Under the current software default, a refund on a commissionable payment is **held for founder review**; nothing is deducted automatically. Whether earned commission is adjusted after a refund is an open legal and accounting decision.

## Withdrawals and payment

Withdrawal requests are built but **not operational**: no frequency, minimum, invoicing or VAT policy is approved. *[FOUNDER DECISION]*

## Planned rewards (not payable)

Achievement rewards and the £250 partner referral reward are **planned and conditional**. The software refuses to approve any reward until a programme version is approved in writing. Do not mention them to anyone as earnings.

## Markets

No market is approved yet, including the UK. A contract cannot be accepted for a customer in an unapproved market. GBP only.

# R08 Objection-handling playbook

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | `DRAFT`; each entry needs individual approval |
| Audience | Partner only, with client-facing lines marked |
| Review owner | Both founders |
| Sources | faq library (keys cited per entry), `published-starting-prices.ts`, [DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md](../../intelligence/DISCOUNT-ALLOWANCES.md) |

Method: **acknowledge, clarify, answer, confirm.** Never resolve an objection with a discount, a guarantee, a timeline or a price that is not published.

| ID | Objection | Clarifying question | Partner guidance | Client-facing line | Escalate when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AP-OBJ-01` | "It's too expensive." | "Compared with what, and for what scope?" | Explain the starting-price boundary, phasing and the audit. Never discount; allowances are disabled and founder-only *[PROPOSED POLICY]* | "The starting price is an entry point for an agreed scope. A proposal lists exactly what's included, and work can be phased. If you'd like a lower-cost first step, the Business Growth Audit is £395." | The client asks for a specific discount or payment plan → commercial assistance | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-02` | "We already have an agency." | "What's working well with them?" | Respect the relationship. Offer a second opinion only | "That's fine. ScaleSmiths always starts by looking at what already works. An audit gives you an independent view, and the findings are useful whoever does the work." | Client complains about the current supplier → do not engage; escalation | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-03` | "Can you guarantee page one?" (faq:ranking-guarantees) | "What would page one mean for the business?" | Never promise rankings, traffic or revenue | "No honest agency can promise a position, because rankings depend on Google, competitors and the searcher. What ScaleSmiths commits to is the work, and measuring progress against a baseline." | Never | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-04` | "We use WordPress / Wix / Shopify." (faq:wordpress, faq:ecommerce-builds) | "What do you like about it?" | Not anti-platform | "ScaleSmiths looks at what your current platform does well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified. Sometimes improving what you have is the better decision." | Migration discussed → technical scoping | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-05` | "How long will it take?" (faq:timeline) | "Is there a date you're working towards?" | Never give a timeline | "Timing is confirmed after discovery, because content readiness and integrations affect it more than page count. The proposal records the range and the assumptions." | Hard deadline → joint sales or technical scoping | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-06` | "Will we lose our rankings?" (faq:seo-rebuild, *owner review*) | "Which pages bring you customers today?" | Acknowledge risk honestly | "Any rebuild carries some risk, and nobody can guarantee rankings. ScaleSmiths reduces it by mapping old pages to new ones, keeping content that performs and checking indexing after launch." | Always for migrations → technical scoping | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-07` | "We need to think about it." | "What would help you decide?" | Respect it; summarise; follow up once on an agreed date | "Of course. I'll send a short summary of what we discussed, and check back on [date] if that's alright." | Never | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-08` | "Who owns the website?" (faq:website-ownership) | — | Use published wording only | "Ownership is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once the agreed fees are paid. You keep your own content, trademarks and data." | Specific contract question → commercial assistance | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-09` | "Can't you just do it cheaper with AI?" | "What would you want it to do?" | Do not disparage AI or oversell it | "AI tools can help with some tasks, but a site still needs accurate content, solid foundations and someone accountable for it. ScaleSmiths uses automation where it genuinely helps." | Never | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-10` | "Are you employed by ScaleSmiths?" | — | Be accurate about independence | "I'm an independent partner of ScaleSmiths. ScaleSmiths scopes, contracts and delivers the work directly." | Never | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (`AP-GOV-05` title) |
| `AP-OBJ-11` | "Do you do hosting / email too?" (faq:hosting-provided, faq:business-email) | "What do you use now?" | Published facts only | "Yes. Hosting can be part of a build or a managed service, and Managed Business Email starts from £15 a month for three mailboxes, with setup included." | DNS or email delivery problems now → technical scoping | `DRAFT` |
| `AP-OBJ-12` | "We're not ready yet." | "What would need to change?" | Accept it; offer a resource; no pressure | "No problem. I can send you a short guide, and you're welcome to get in touch when the time is right." | Never | `DRAFT` |

# Empower design specification

**Status: DRAFT.** Visual direction for the Academy, Resource Centre and founder publishing interface. Screen-level layouts are in [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md). Brand changes need founder approval (`AP-DES-01`).

## 1. Direction

**Quiet premium.** Black and charcoal surfaces, metallic gold used sparingly as a signal of quality and of "approved", silver for secondary emphasis, generous spacing, clear typography, minimal navigation. The interface should feel calm and trustworthy: a partner is about to speak to a client and needs the right answer fast. Search comes first; decoration never competes with content.

Principles:

1. **Content first.** Text measures 60 to 75 characters on large screens; nothing decorative inside reading areas.
2. **Gold means something.** Gold marks primary actions, the active item and approval ribbons. It is not used for body text or large fills.
3. **Status is never colour alone.** Every status has a text label and an icon.
4. **Mobile is a first-class target.** Partners will read lessons and look up answers on phones before meetings.

# Empower design specification

**Status: DRAFT.** Visual direction for the Academy, Resource Centre and founder publishing interface. Screen-level layouts are in [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md). Brand changes need founder approval (`AP-DES-01`).

## 1. Direction

**Quiet premium.** Black and charcoal surfaces, metallic gold used sparingly as a signal of quality and of "approved", silver for secondary emphasis, generous spacing, clear typography, minimal navigation. The interface should feel calm and trustworthy: a partner is about to speak to a client and needs the right answer fast. Search comes first; decoration never competes with content.

Principles:

1. **Content first.** Text measures 60 to 75 characters on large screens; nothing decorative inside reading areas.
2. **Gold means something.** Gold marks primary actions, the active item and approval ribbons. It is not used for body text or large fills.
3. **Status is never colour alone.** Every status has a text label and an icon.
4. **Mobile is a first-class target.** Partners will read lessons and look up answers on phones before meetings.
5. **Reuse before invent.** Build on the admin tokens and the `ex-*` portal patterns.

## 2. Reconciling the two existing systems

The Partner Portal is part of the admin app, so Empower uses the **admin token set** as its base and borrows silver from the public site. It does not import the public site's warm palette wholesale, which would make the portal inconsistent with the rest of the admin shell.

| Role | Empower token | Value | Origin | Contrast (measured) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Page background | `--bg` | `#131416` | admin | — |
| Raised surface | `--s1` | `#1a1b1e` | admin | — |
| Card surface | `--s2` | `#222428` | admin | — |
| Hover surface | `--s3` | `#2a2d31` | admin | — |
| Primary text | `--t1` | `#f1f5f9` | admin | 16.82:1 on `--bg` |
| Secondary text | `--t2` | `#a6b0be` | admin | 7.85:1 on `--s1`; 7.09:1 on `--s2` |
| Muted text (new) | `--emp-muted` | `#939cac` | new (corrected in review from `#8a93a3`, which is 4.47:1 on `--s3` and fails there) | 6.66:1 on `--bg`; 5.62:1 on `--s2`; 5.00:1 on `--s3` |
| Decorative text only | `--t3` | `#667085` | admin | **Fails AA for body text on every admin surface**: 3.71:1 on `--bg`, 3.46:1 on `--s1`, 3.12:1 on `--s2`, 2.78:1 on `--s3`; use only for disabled states and decoration |
| Metallic gold (solid) | `--acc` | `#d1b266` | admin | 9.01:1 on `--bg`; 7.60:1 on `--s2` |
| Gold gradient (decoration) | `--emp-gold` | `linear-gradient(135deg,#e6cf8f 0%,#d1b266 45%,#a8873f 100%)` | new, from `--acc` | Dark text `#131416` on it: 5.44:1 at the darkest stop |
| Silver | `--emp-silver` | `#cfc7bc` | public `--silver` | 11.01:1 on `--bg`; 9.29:1 on `--s2` |
| Silver line | `--emp-silver-line` | `rgba(207,199,188,.18)` | new | — |
| Approved | `--grn` | `#10b981` | admin | 6.79:1 on `--s1` |
| Review due / draft | `--amb` | `#f59e0b` | admin | 8.02:1 on `--s1` |
| Blocked / withdrawn | `--red` | `#ef4444` | admin | 4.58:1 on `--s1`, **4.13:1 on `--s2` (fails for normal text)**; use for icons, rules and large text, with a text label in `--t1` or `--t2` |

Contrast values were calculated with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (the same method as `web/src/lib/color-contrast.ts`). They must be asserted in tests at implementation, as the public site already does.

**Clean-up recommended alongside:** `expansion.css` hard-codes `#131416`, `#18191b`, `#edf0f5` and `#c3a86c`. Empower styles should use tokens only; replacing the hard-coded portal values is a small, separate change (`AP-ENG-05`).

## 3. Typography

| Use | Family | Size / line height | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display (course titles, page titles) | `--font-syne` (admin resolves this to Arial Black) | 28/34 desktop, 24/30 mobile | 700 |
| Section heading | Inter | 20/28 | 600 |
| Body and lesson text | Inter | 17/28 (lesson), 15/24 (UI) | 400 |
| Labels, overlines | Inter, uppercase, letter-spacing .14em | 11/16 | 600 |
| Data and figures | Inter, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (as `.ex-money`) | as context | 500 |

Decision `AP-DES-02`: whether to self-host Syne in the admin app (as the public site does) so display type matches the brand. Until decided, the existing fallback stays.

## 4. Layout and spacing

- 8px spacing grid; page gutter 16px mobile, 24px tablet, 36px desktop (matching `.ex-header`).
- Max content width 1200px; reading column 720px.
- Radius: 8px cards (admin `--radius-md`), 12px feature panels (as `.ex-research`), 999px chips.
- Elevation: borders before shadows; `--shadow-raised` only for overlays.
- Breakpoints: 640px, 960px, 1280px.

## 5. Components

| Component | Specification | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| Portal shell | Existing header and tab navigation. Empower adds three entries: Academy, Resources, Knowledge | `ExpansionWorkspace` items |
| Search bar | Full width, 52px tall, silver 1px border, gold focus ring (3px, `rgba(209,178,102,.28)`), keyboard shortcut `/` | `.field-control` pattern |
| Course card | `--s2` surface, 2px gold-gradient top edge, overline (course number), title, one-line purpose, lesson count and reading time, progress ring (private), status chip | `.ex-panel` |
| Status chip | Pill with icon and text: Approved · v3 · review by 12 Mar 2027; Partner only; Client-facing; Updated since you read it | `.ex-badge` |
| Audience ribbon | Full-width strip above content: silver "Partner only: do not share" or gold-outlined "Client-facing: approved for sharing" | new |
| Lesson body | Reading column, 17px text, callouts for "Say it like this" (gold left rule), "Avoid" (red left rule, labelled), "Escalate when" (silver left rule) | new |
| Knowledge result | Question (heading), client explanation (first), limitation, escalation, source, status chip | new |
| Copy control | Only on client-facing text; announces "Copied" via `aria-live` | new |
| Empty state | One sentence and a next action, as in the existing `Empty` component | `Empty` |
| Founder diff view | Side-by-side or inline diff between versions, additions in green, removals struck through, with labels | new |

## 6. Motion

Subtle and optional: 150 to 200ms fades for panels and chips, no parallax, no animated gradients. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (the admin already does for its workspace).

## 7. Accessibility requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA as the target for these screens (an engineering target, not a public claim).
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, logical heading order, skip link to search.
- Status conveyed by text and icon as well as colour.
- Lesson text resizable to 200% without horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- Knowledge checks: answers announced via `aria-live`; no time limits.

lines: Contrast values were calculated with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (the same method as `web/src/lib/color-contrast.ts`). They must be asserted in tests at implementation, as the public site already does.

+**Admin-wide muted text (`AP-DES-03`).** `--t3` is not only an Empower concern: at planning time it is used through `var(--t3)` 68 times in 36 admin files (mostly the Forge panels, Dashboard, Clients, Kanban, Messages and ProspectPipeline) and through the Tailwind `text-t3` class 72 times in 15 files. Changing the global token would alter all of them. Recommendation: Empower uses `--emp-muted` only; a separate, founder-approved change raises `--t3` to `#939cac` (or retires it for text) with screenshot comparison of the affected screens and the contrast assertions above. Do not change the global token inside an Empower PR.

**Clean-up recommended alongside:** `expansion.css` hard-codes `#131416`, `#18191b`, `#edf0f5` and `#c3a86c`. Empower styles should use tokens only; replacing the hard-coded portal values is a small, separate change (`AP-ENG-05`).
